item.title: Big Ten standings through Week 10: Six teams tied for third place
item.description: There seems to be two clear frontrunners in the Big Ten after Ohio State's shocking loss to Oregon. The Buckeyes dropped to 4-2 in conference play and are now part of a massive six-team tie for third place. Obviously, the Big Ten Championship game is only played between the top two teams in the conference, so the Buckeyes could be out of the picture entirely if UCLA and Indiana keep up at this pace. OSU is joined by Oregon, Iowa , Wisconsin , USC, and Illinois in a tight-knit group of teams vying to compete for a conference championship if either the Bruins or Hoosiers slip up. With three games remianing, it's also worth keeping an eye on Northwestern and Minnesota who are 3-3. Big Ten football standings through Week 10 UCLA Bruins (6-0) Indiana Hoosiers (5-1) Oregon Ducks (4-2) Ohio State Buckeyes (4-2) Iowa Hawkeyes (4-2) Wisconsin Badgers (4-2) USC Trojans (4-2) Illinois Fighting Illini (4-2) Northwestern Wildcats (3-3) Minnesota Golden Gophers (3-3) Penn State Nittany Lions (2-4) Washington Huskies (2-4) Michigan Wolverines (2-4) Nebraska Cornhuskers (2-4) Purdue Boilermakers (2-4) Rutgers Scarlet Knights (1-5) Maryland Terrapins (1-5) Michigan State Spartans (1-5) Contact/Follow @TheBadgersWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Wisconsin Badgers news, notes and opinion. item.title: Senne Lammens Is Becoming A Problem For Manchester United
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 3: Senne Lammens, goalkeeper of Manchester United on the pitch during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford on November 3, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images) Getty Images There is no more chaotic team in the Premier League right now than Manchester United. Fresh from staging a Champions League comeback against Roma, fighting back from 2-0 down to win 3-2, Michael Carrick’s side staged another comeback on Sunday, dramatically drawing 4-4 with Aston Villa having trailed by two goals twice. It was a performance that showed the strengths and weaknesses of the Old Trafford outfit. In the attack, United dug deep to find the back of the net four times with the likes of Matheus Cunha, Patrick Dorgu and Joshua Zirkzee all making an impact in the final third when their team needed them to. MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Michael Carrick, Manager of Manchester United, during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford on November 08, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Getty Images Defensively, though, Sunday’s match was yet another shambles. Villa scored four times and could have scored more. Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro all contributed to a mess of a performance at the back, but Senne Lammens was possibly the biggest culprit of all. Indeed, Lammens was at fault for the opening goal of the match which came from Alysson less than a minute after kick-off. The Belgian goalkeeper might also have done better for the second goal which was scored by Nicolas Jackson after a speculative shot was spilled by Lammens. Last season, Lammens was a big upgrade for Manchester United in the goalkeeper position. Signed from Royal Antwerp as something of an unknown, the Belgian quickly established himself in the number one position at Old Trafford and earned himself a reputation for being one of the best goalkeepers in the English top flight. Manchester, United Kingdom - November 3: Senne Lammens of Manchester United during the UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 match between Manchester United and Roma at Old Trafford on November 3, 2026 in Manchester, United Kingdom. (Photo by Ryan Crockett/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) DeFodi Images via Getty Images Recently, though, Lammens has allowed mistakes to creep into his game. The 24-year-old’s shot-stopping has been suspect, as has his handling from set pieces and crosses. Lammens’ performances are spreading nervousness within the Manchester United defensive ranks at the worst possible time. Carrick’s future is up in the air after a run of just one win in 10 games in all competitions for United. The club’s ownership and leadership have backed the former midfielder this far, but the reality is that Manchester United enters the November international window in the relegation

item.title: ‘It’s called bodybuilding, not plastic building’: Champ alleges fake muscles
item.description: Four-time women's bodybuilding champion Sarah Villegas recently granted an exclusive interview to USA TODAY Sports about a massive controversy that's shaken up her sport. She has accused rival Natalia Coelho of getting injected with a Plexiglas substance to build fake "plastic" muscles before winning the Ms. Olympia event for best women’s physique in 2025. She made this claim after obtaining unsolicited "firsthand" information about it from a licensed health professional at the clinic in Brazil where the procedure allegedly took place. USA TODAY reviewed this information and confirmed with this person that they shared it with Villegas. The person didn't want to be identified for fear of retaliation. Injecting Plexiglass? A champion cried foul. Bodybuilding’s response raises more questions Coelho hasn’t denied or confirmed the allegation and didn't return messages seeking comment. Coelho again won the crown for best physique at Ms. Olympia in September, beating Villegas for the second year in a row. The Olympia event is the "Super Bowl" of pro bodybuilding. Here is the interview with Villegas. What caused you to suspect this with Natalia Coelho? Villegas: I first became suspicious and spoke up publicly on this when I noticed what I thought was an abrupt change in Natalia Coelho's legs at the 2025 Pittsburgh Pro, just a few months before the 2025 Olympia. I was still the reigning and defending Olympia Champion at the time. I had noticed that her legs changed their natural genetic shape, and displayed what I thought was a humanly impossible change in volume in a very short period of time. Why did you go public initially? (Villegas posted a message on Instagram about her suspicions last year and followed up with more after that . Some described her as a "sore loser" in response.) Villegas: I went public to bring attention to what I think is an existential issue. Existential to the future of the sport of bodybuilding and to the future of my own career. In my opinion, the sport of bodybuilding will not survive for long if a world champion can stand on stage displaying muscles that aren't actually muscle. Did you suspect it was PMMA (Plexiglas) before getting information about it from the clinic worker? (PMMA is polymethyl methacrylate, also known commercially as Plexiglas. PMMA microspheres have been used for dermal filler treatments in some countries but recently were banned for that purpose in Brazil.) Villegas: No I did not. Before the doctor came forward to me, I thought it was site enhancement oil. You first brought the PMMA allegations to the attention of the IFBB Pro League privately? (The IFBB Pro League is the sport’s governing body and was originally known as the International Federation of Body Builders.) item.title: Eagles players met with Nick Sirianni in his office after losing to the Giants
item.description: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles dropped their seventh game in a row on Sunday, losing to the Giants in a game that capped off a losing NFC East trifecta for the Birds in as many weeks. Reporters had to wait quite a while to talk to head coach Nick Sirianni after the game. Sirianni didn’t start his post-game press conference until about 72 minutes after the final whistle of Sunday’s game. When he was asked about it – since it’s pretty unusual for him to take that long – he explained that he was talking to players. “Talking to some guys, talking to some players. Those guys — everyone puts everything they have into this, so I want to make sure I talk to every guy first of all after the game. Then a couple of the guys stopped in the office just to talk through it. That’s not unusual. I appreciate the connection that we have there.” Here’s what else the head coach had to say: On Joe Milton’s performance “I think just like everybody, [Joe Milton] had some really good plays and then he’s going to have plays that he’s going to want back, naturally. But I thought he did a lot of good things, a lot of solid things, made some plays with his feet, gave our guys a couple chances downfield. Thought he was good in the play action world. I thought he did some really nice things. Obviously, we have to play better complimentary football to be able to have the run game coincide with the play actions that we were running, but there were some good things that he had.” On the 4th-and-1 play call Sirianni said that they had some time to think about the fourth-and-one call, and they were debating between a couple different options. Ultimately, the head coach was good with the call and with what they ended up running. “Obviously, it didn’t work. So, we’ll go back to the drawing board in there on that play. But there was a lot of time to think about that call because again, we got on the ball, it went to a two-minute warning, had a lot of time there, and obviously it didn’t work. So, we’ll go back and see what we can do differently offensively.” On the QB protection When asked about the unblocked sack-fumble, Sirianni said he wasn’t going to get into who was at fault, but did acknowledge that anytime there’s a guy that’s free in that situation, they have to look at the coaching to see what went wrong. He noted that it becomes an execution issue after they sort out the coaching issue, so it’s on everyone to get it fixed. “Obviously in that case, we’ll make those corrections in person with everybody. Whether it’s on us as coaches or whether it’s an execution thing, it’s still on us as coaches. It starts with me and it’s always on me; every product that’s on that field is my responsibility. ‘Well, there was an execution error on this play or that play.’ Well, did I put him in every position I could possibly put him into to go out and execute that?” On potential coaching changes “We’ll talk. item.title: Bruins' First 18 Games Reveal Some Remarkable Numbers Behind Boston's Hot Start
item.description: Bruins' First 18 Games Reveal Some Remarkable Numbers Behind Boston's Hot Start originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins have completed 18 games of the 2026-27 NHL season, and their early success is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook. Boston improved to 13-4-1 with Sunday's 4-1 victory over the Florida Panthers, extending its winning streak to four games. The Bruins have collected 27 of a possible 36 standings points, putting them atop the Atlantic Division and among the NHL's strongest teams. The record is impressive, but several underlying numbers provide an even better explanation of what has made Boston so successful. Boston's Goal Differential Tells A Powerful Story Through 18 games, the Bruins have scored 67 goals while allowing only 41, producing an impressive plus-26 goal differential. That works out to approximately 3.72 goals scored and 2.28 goals allowed per game, a combination that gives Boston a considerable advantage on most nights. A fine day from start to finish 👋 https://t.co/skIkUCHSvk — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) November 8, 2026 The Bruins rank among the league leaders in both categories, demonstrating that their success has not depended entirely on one side of the ice. Boston has been capable of generating offense while limiting opponents' scoring opportunities, making the team difficult to beat when both elements are working together. Bruins Have Responded To Every Setback Boston opened the season 7-2-1 through 10 games, including a five-game winning streak in October. The Bruins then experienced another difficult stretch with consecutive losses to Carolina and St. Louis, but their response has been encouraging. They have won four straight games since October 31, defeating Chicago, Vegas, Pittsburgh and Florida. Sunday's victory was particularly impressive because Jeremy Swayman stopped 40 shots, helping Boston control the scoreboard despite facing considerable pressure. MORE : Nikita Zadorov, Brady Tkachuk Immediately Drop Gloves, Start Bruins vs. Panthers With Fight Bruins Are Building Something Worth Watching Boston's early success has involved contributions from several players rather than one offensive star carrying the entire workload. The team has also demonstrated the ability to win in different ways, including high-scoring performances, defensive battles and overtime contests. The next challenge is maintaining that consistency as the schedule becomes more demanding. Boston returns to action Thursday against Montreal, with another opportunity to strengthen its position in the Atlantic Division. Eighteen games do not guarantee how an entire season will unfold, but the Bruins have already established an impressive foundation. Their combination of scoring, defense and resilience suggests this start deserves attention. item.title: It will happen eventually: El Mala drops a transfer hint
item.description: It will happen eventually: El Mala drops a transfer hint Despite receiving numerous offers last summer, 20-year-old Said El Mala decided to stay at 1. FC Köln and sign a long-term contract extension until 2031. Now the Germany international has explained the reasons behind his decision. Speaking to RTL and Sky, the forward reflected on the transfer window: “I chose Köln because I simply felt at home here. I didn’t want to leave, even though there were a lot of inquiries.” He made no secret in the interview of having considered offers from other clubs: “Of course, we listened to everything. That’s completely normal.” Ultimately, however, the club’s sporting prospects tipped the balance in favor of staying. Speaking to the two TV broadcasters, El Mala explained: “But I spoke a lot with the board and the coach and listened to their plans for the team. Looking at things now, those plans have been put into practice exactly as discussed. I want to make the city and the club happy through my performances and those of the team.” There was certainly no shortage of high-profile suitors in the summer. Among them, English Premier League club Brighton & Hove Albion sounded out a move for the youngster. Borussia Dortmund were also reportedly prepared to put a transfer fee of around €50 million on the table, but Köln’s management felt that was too little. Given his potential, keeping the forward at Köln for the long term is considered unlikely. Asked about his future career ambitions by RTL and Sky, the 20-year-old made an eye-catching statement: “There are always dreams. I want to achieve a lot one day and play in the Champions League too. I can’t say when that moment will come. But it will happen someday.” This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: A C.J. Stroud flu game? Sick and with the chills, Texans QB throws for 5 TDs to beat Chargers
item.description: Back in his native Southern California, C.J. Stroud turned in one of the best games of his career as the Texans stayed in the playoff hunt with a win over the Chargers. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) INGLEWOOD, Calif. - When C.J. Stroud woke up in his hotel bed Sunday morning in downtown Los Angeles, he was still feeling under the weather. All week he had been dealing with some kind of illness that he said gave him chills and "all the things." He said he barely practiced Thursday. Whatever he had, it was still with him. Yet, some six hours later, he went on to have one of the best games of his career. Stroud, who was playing in front of friends and family near his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga , threw for a season-high 384 yards, a career-high five touchdowns and just one interception in Houston's 44-22 rout of the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The 44 points scored were a season high for the Texans' offense, which has often delivered time and time again, especially on the road. The Texans improved to 3-5 on the season. It was the type of performance that will put Stroud in the MVP conversation if he can continue playing this way. It is the type of performance that will have some suggesting that the Texans can make a run towards the playoffs. "He really gives that confidence to the entire team," coach DeMeco Ryans said of Stroud. "When the defensive guys, they see him up making plays, everyone is excited. Everyone knows the type of energy, the type of momentum that that brings to our entire team when he's making those plays and he's done it all year." The Texans are currently 1 ½ games behind the Patriots for that final wild-card spot with nine games remaining. They face the Browns, who are also 1 ½ games ahead of them, next Sunday in Cleveland. But based on their upcoming schedule, and how Stroud is playing, anything is possible, especially if the defense can gain some momentum too. Though the performance from the defense wasn't perfect, Sunday's game against the NFL's worst offense was a step in the right direction. The Texans tied a franchise record with eight sacks on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. They also forced two turnovers - an interception by cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. and a fumble. But the offense, which had 485 yards of total offense, was the story of this game. And it started with Stroud, who became just the fourth quarterback younger than 26 years old with at least 350 passing yards and five touchdown passes in multiple games, joining Patrick Mahomes, Dan Marino and Matthew Stafford. The other game Stroud achieved that stat line was during his 2023 rookie season, when he threw five touchdowns in a thrilling 39-37 win over the Bucs . item.title: 3 Former Top Prospects The Pirates Should Sign For Depth
item.description: Jun 2, 2024; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Braves outfielder Jarred Kelenic (24) runs to first base after hitting a ground ball against the Oakland Athletics during the eighth inning at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Godfree-USA T… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Evan Mazza, Site Editor Good MLB teams have good depth. Having someone interesting at Triple-A that a team can call up in a pinch is always a must. The Pittsburgh Pirates always need depth stashed at Triple-A, and what better way than to give a former top prospect a chance as a change-of-scenery candidate ? With dozens of players recently hitting minor league free agency , the Pirates should take a zero-risk chance on a former top prospect on a minor league contract. At worst, the Pirates sign a player who serves solely as Triple-A depth; at best, they find a diamond in the rough and unlock something the former prospect’s previous team couldn’t. Heston Kjerstad Would Be a Great Fit for the Pirates Heston Kjerstad entered the 2020 draft as one of the best players available and was selected second overall by the Baltimore Orioles. By 2024, he was a consensus top 50 prospect and was looking to make an impact in MLB. Things got off to a promising start for Kjerstad, as he hit for a 113 wRC+ over his first 147 MLB plate appearances in 2023 and 2024. Apr 30, 2025; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Orioles outfielder Heston Kjerstad (13) hits a single during the eighth inning against the New York Yankees at Oriole Park at Camden Yards. Mandatory Credit: Reggie Hildred-Imagn Images However, Kjerstad failed to capture a regular role in 2025. In 167 plate appearances, the outfielder hit just .192/.240/.328 with a .248 wOBA and 57 wRC+. He only hit four home runs while striking out over a quarter of the time (26.9%). However, the most worrying part of his first chance at regular playing time was his 3.6% walk rate. Kjerstad spent most of 2026 in the minor leagues, appearing in just 11 MLB games, and struggled to a 28 wRC+ over the small sample size. The O’s released Kjerstad at the end of the season. Although Kjerstad has struggled in his brief MLB time, he has done nothing but hit Triple-A pitching. In 1040 plate appearances dating back to his first look at Triple-A in 2023, the former second overall pick is batting .279/.351/.482 with a .365 wOBA and 115 wRC+. He has walked in 8.6% of his plate appearances, with a 23.9% K%. Kjerstad has plenty of raw power, as indicated by his 89.6 MPH exit velocity; however, his 27% whiff rate is a tad high. Kjerstad, who is primarily an outfielder, also has nearly 400 professional innings at first base. The former top prospect could provide the Pirates with depth at multiple positions. item.title: Former Cardinals Infielder Announces Return In New Role Immediately After Retirement
item.description: ST. LOUIS, MO - SEPTEMBER 8: Jose Martinez #58 of the St. Louis Cardinals hits a two-run single against the Pittsburgh Pirates in the fifth inning at Busch Stadium on September 8, 2017 in St. Louis, Missouri. (Photo by Dilip Vishwanat/Getty Images) Getty Images The St. Louis Cardinals seemed to make some progress on identifying core members of their team’s near-term future, but the team missed the postseason for the fourth straight season as a lengthy rebuild continues. As the team works its way back toward contention, fans got an update from a member of the team’s more successful recent history, as a longtime position player who had a memorable run in St. Louis is now preparing to take a new step in his baseball career. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers’ Recent Rookie Standout Cuts Ties With New Team After Very Short Stint Former St Louis Cardinals Sparplug Joins AL Organization After Retirement Jose Martinez, better known to many Cardinals fans as “Cafecito,” has announced that he is joining the Minnesota Twins organization in a new capacity, marking his return to affiliated baseball shortly after retiring as a player. “Today I am filled with pride to share with you that I am beginning a new stage as a hitting coach in the Minnesota Twins organization,” Martinez wrote in a translated version of the announcement . “Today it is my turn to share what I learned as a ballplayer and to help others build their own path.” The announcement represents a transition for the former Cardinals fan favorite, who spent much of his major-league career in St. Louis before eventually making stops with the Tampa Bay Rays and Chicago Cubs. Martinez’s professional playing career continued internationally after he left the Cubs. And now his decision to move into coaching gives him an opportunity to pass along the experience he accumulated throughout those years. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Castoff Trevor Bauer Offers 5-Word Response On Yankees Reunion Post St Louis Cardinals Career, Retirement Lead To New Minnesota Twins Hire “Martinez concluded his playing career in 2025 after a run in the Mexican League and winter ball in his native Venezuela,” Anthony Franco wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . “Martínez played five seasons in the big leagues. He’s best known for his 2016-19 run with the Cardinals, for whom he had a trio of double digit home run seasons.” Martinez finished his major-league career with 43 home runs, 182 RBI and a .289 batting average across 432 games. His most productive stretch came in St. Louis, where he became a useful offensive contributor and demonstrated the ability to hit for average while providing occasional power. The Twins’ decision to bring Martínez into their organization offers him a different avenue to remain involved in the game. Rather than continuing to compete on the field, he will now work to develop hitters and help the next generation of professional players. item.title: Michigan Football needs to start planning for a future without Kyle Whittingham
item.description: Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham looks up at the scoreboard during second half action at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Michigan State won the game 15-6. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Over the offseason, excitement built steadily for the 2026 Michigan football season. There were plenty of reasons for optimism with Kyle Whittingham coming in to take over the program. One of the winningest coaches of the 21st century was finally getting the chance to prove himself in a place that’s well-resourced and always has a stream of talent. Instead, the fan base had the wool pulled over its eyes, Michigan’s administration got duped, and the program sits in as bad a place as it’s been since the turn of the century. The idea of hiring Whittingham made a lot of sense last December. Rocked by scandals over the last few years, Michigan needed someone who could stabilize things and be an “adult in the room” while also bringing in enough football acumen to help turn a talented roster into a winner in short order. The “short order” part is key due to Whittingham’s age. At 66, it was clear he’d be in Ann Arbor for only a few years before finally retiring, giving it one last shot to go for a national title. With as much talent as Michigan already had on its roster and the nine wins it had in 2025, no ramp-up was needed. But instead, the team has taken several steps back and looks nowhere close to where it was even at this time last year. This has been most evident over Michigan’s last two games: a sleepy seven-point win at Rutgers, and Saturday’s debacle in which the Wolverines looked totally uninspired and unprepared against a 3-6 Michigan State team. There are three games left, but it’s apparent Michigan has mailed it in, with three more losses surely coming. Michigan’s season going off the rails like this is unfathomable if you think about how much optimism there was just three months ago and how many good pieces were in place. However, it’s not a total surprise if you’ve watched college football for any length of time. There have been plenty of teams that come into the year in similar situations with good rosters and coaching staffs only to see that optimism dwindle at the first signs of adversity. Perhaps this has been amplified over the last few years, with the portal bringing together teams full of players who don’t have deep ties to one another and less loyalty to their schools than ever before. Programs like Florida State, Texas A&M, Penn State, Oklahoma, Clemson and Florida have all had major expectations in recent years and seen their seasons go down in flames by mid-October, with Michigan joining them this season. While the Wolverines certainly belong on that list of programs that have fallen from grace, they’re also a bit of an outlier, having won a national championship just three years ago. They also don’t have a young head coach who’s simply going through growing pains — they have someone who was supposed to be the an

item.title: Cowboys news: Dallas avoids another late-game upset, winning late over the Colts
item.description: Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images | Getty Images If there is one thing that fans can rely on this season, it’s that Dallas will keep things interesting. Even with the win, the Cowboys and their front office still need to make a decision on what the goal for this season is and how much they trust the current staff to achieve that goal. In a postgame interview, Dak Prescott acknowledged that this win was crucial. The Cowboys don’t need to run the table to make the playoffs this season; however, games like this are necessary today and going forward. Time will tell if Dallas is able to get the job done in those crucial games, but on Sunday, they got the job done. Cowboys 27 – Colts 23: How Tough is this Dallas Team?- Cody Warren, Inside The Star A chronological recap of the game. Dak’s throw to Jonathan Mingo on the opening drive was great. Third-and-3, George Pickens out, and Dak goes down the middle to Mingo for 23 yards. Imagine being the Colts and having to account for Mingo the rest of the game because you gave him that much room while CeeDee Lamb was on the field. A few uneventful plays to Javonte Williams and you just gave Brandon Aubrey a shorter field goal. 8 instant takeaways from Cowboys’ ugly win over the Colts in Week 9- Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat Caleb Downs is starting to make a bigger impact. Downs does so many things well, and blitzing is one of them. Whether it’s due to injuries in the secondary or Christian Parker simply being overwhelmed as a first-time play-caller, he has not blitzed his star rookie nearly enough this season. Parker went back to that well on 3rd-and-8 early in the second quarter. Downs came flying off the edge and buried Daniel Jones for a 10-yard loss to force a punt . Jones never saw him coming. It was a free shot, so you almost wish Downs had managed to jar the ball loose, but that’s nitpicking what was an outstanding play by the rookie. Dak Prescott, Cowboys offense persevere vs. Colts: ‘We had to have it’- Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Dak Prescott is well aware this team will have their backs up against the wall for the remainder of the season. With a Giants team ahead of them that keeps winning, Dallas will need to do the same. “You get a chance, you got to go win it, you got to go finish it,” Prescott said. “There’s going to be some ups and downs, we can’t ride them, we’ve got to stay focused and stay locked into whatever our job is individually and it’s important collectively. At the end of the game, when you’ve got an opportunity to win or to close them out, you’ve got to do it, you can’t let up.” Download the SB Nation app today! item.title: New York Jets News: David Bailey Provides Historic Silver Lining in Loss to Chiefs
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) passes the ball against the New York Jets during the second quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Stop the presses: the New York Jets lost again. The Jets flirted with a potential upset in the first half, but familiar problems plagued them: penalties, settling for field goals, and dumb mistakes. Instead of talking about the fourth straight loss in what looks like another dumpster-fire season, let’s highlight a positive, shall we? David Bailey is a freaking superstar. He finished the game with two sacks, three tackles for loss, three quarterback hits, and nine total tackles. Bailey has the third most sacks in the league (7.5), the second most tackles for loss (11), and he is first in the league in forced fumbles (five). This is a foundational building block for the next decade plus. Sure, that Arvell Reese guy is having a hell of a season with the New York Giants, but why can’t both guys be good? Why do we have to constantly compare and contrast? Oh, this guy is great, and oh, this guy stinks. I saw all that noise on social media during and after the game. Just imagine how much better Bailey will be when he has a secondary that can intercept passes, and he has a better running mate on the other side of him. This talented player is only scratching the surface of his true potential at the NFL level. J-E-T-S! Take the game-day conversation with you! item.title: Browns vs. Texans odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup
item.description: The Cleveland Browns opened as 4.5-point home underdogs against the Houston Texans ahead of their Week 10 match-up, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under on the game is 39.5. The Browns (5-4) are coming off of a 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . It was a one week start for Shedeur Sanders , and for three quarters, the offense looked quite ugly. Once he let loose and started airing the ball downfield, though, the offense came alive. Unfortunately, that also involved the Saints putting their first touchdowns on the board. In overtime, the Browns answered the Saints’ touchdown, but with a minute to go, they tried to go for the win (a two-point try) instead of settling for a tie or loss. They didn’t get it, and lost their second straight game. Deshaun Watson will return to start against the Texans. The Texans (3-5) are coming off of a 44-22 victory over the winless Chargers. C.J. Stroud had five touchdown passes and 384 passing yards in the win. Houston has been an odd team to get a pulse on. They are 0-4 at home, 3-1 on the road, and began the year with four straight losses before winning three of their last four. Statistically, they’ve been good at throwing the ball, but also bad at defending the passing game. Either way, it seems a little ‘off’ that the Browns are at home, yet one of the largest underdogs they’ve been all season. The over/under for the game is 39.5. What odds would you take if you were placing a bet?

item.title: 'Make every state your own.' Texas football relishes SEC road trips like win vs Missouri
item.description: Texas Longhorns defensive back Graceson Littleton (29) and Texas Longhorns linebacker Justin Cryer (28) defend Missouri Tigers wide receiver Cayden Lee (19) during the game against Missouri at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) COLUMBIA, Mo. - The chatter started before Texas football even joined the SEC. The conference is too rugged, the league's old guard said. The road trips are too grueling. And the Longhorns, with their abundance of resources and Big 12 background, are just too soft. But as the team proved yet again in Saturday's 34-20 win at No. 18 Missouri, No. 7 Texas (7-2, 4-2 SEC) has the steel needed for a run at the College Football Playoff. The Longhorns improved to 7-2 in true SEC road games since joining the conference in 2024, a rate of success that must impress even the most ardent burnt-orange skeptic. "Our guys, they're not naive to noise," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said after Saturday's win. "As much as I would love to say, ‘Hey, tune it all out,' I could hear the talk getting on the plane (Friday). I could hear the talk when we got here. Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage. Everyone thought we'd get pushed around." MORE: Texas football shows it can win tough road games - and play team ball - at Mizzou | Golden Texas Longhorns tight end Emaree Winston (85) jumps over Missouri Tigers safety Kensley Louidor-Faustin (7) as he carries the ball in the second quarter during the game against Missouri at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Steve Sarkisian: Pack defense, pack run game for road trips UP NEXT NO. 7 TEXAS AT NO. 14 LSU When/where: 6:30 p.m. Saturday in Baton Rouge, La. TV/radio: ABC; 1300 AM, 98.1 FM, 105.3 FM. For the record, Texas entered the game as a 3½-point betting favorite. But Sarkisian's point holds water; Missouri (6-3, 3-3) entered the game with its own hopes of a CFP spot because of its dominance on both lines of scrimmage, and the Longhorns had lingering concerns about their own rushing attack as well as holding up against the run. But in a slugfest that felt much closer than the final score, Texas ran for 107 yards on 23 carries before taking away sacks yardage and held the SEC's leading rusher in Jamal Roberts to 66 yards on 19 carries. "It's the old adage, right? When you go on the road, you want to pack a defense and you want to pack your run game," Sarkisian said. "We packed a few more things; we felt like we needed more than that. But those two ingredients always give you a chance." In the process, the Longhorns silenced a sold-out crowd at Memorial Stadium that craved a win over its former Big 12 tormentor. item.title: METROCARD SWIPE: 5 Takeaways from the America East-Metro Challenge
item.description: The November 9 MetroCard Swipe with takeaways from the America East-Metro Challenge. | Photo by Fairfield Athletics / Design by Hannah Butler (Mid-Major Madness) This story was going to be a continuation of last week’s story with how poorly Thursday went for the Metro. The conference went 3-6 in the home games of the America East-Metro Challenge, setting itself up for a tough mountain to climb on Sunday. But to the league’s credit, they climbed that mountain. The Metro won a bunch of close games to go 5-3 on Sunday, setting up a chance to tie the Challenge should Iona defeat UMBC a week from Monday. Instead of straight doom, here are five takeaways from the Metro-America East Challenge. Dywane Chess is Marist’s most important player John Dunne went out of his way to say that he’s extremely high on freshman Dywane Chess during our preseason interview. He’s looked the part of a Metro Rookie of the Year candidate thanks to his scoring through three games. He dropped 20 points in both of Marist’s America East-Metro Challenge games, leading the Red Foxes in scoring both times. His usage rate through three games is 27.5%, the highest on the team, and he’s played 75% of the team’s minutes as well. Jack Graham and Edward Onyia have taken lower-usage roles than I expected, and Myles Parker still isn’t putting the ball on the floor a ton, so the offensive burden will fall on Chess throughout the year. There will be some games where Brady MacAdams gives Marist a lift – like on Thursday night when he made three triples and scored 17 points – but Chess will have to be the night-in, night-out guy. Chess has a strong frame at 6-foot-4 and has the green light to create off the dribble. He’s already assuming the role of creating mid-range jump shots and getting plenty of spot-up opportunities. I wonder if more pick-and-roll reps are coming as he starts to adapt into a hybrid between the Justin Menard and Elijah Lewis roles. But this all begs the question: will Graham, Onyia, and Parker come along? Graham was solid in the Challenge, but presumably has more in him. Onyia was held scoreless and limited to just 12 minutes in each of the Challenge games. Can those guys give Chess a little more support than they have so far? Quinnipiac’s backcourt is fun Sunday’s win over Vermont was by far the best game of Tai Turnage’s college career. He took five 3s, and he made five 3s, and he has already drilled more than a third as many triples as he did all of last season. In the second half against the Catamounts, Turnage was confidently launching bombs whenever Vermont went under his screens. He finished with 17 points, but also six assists and zero turnovers. Meanwhile, Tayeshawn Cunningham-Pemberton played a really strong two-way game against Bryant, scoring 17 points himself. He made a few key plays and showed off his toughness against Vermont on Sunday as well. item.title: Orioles news: O’s prospects play in AFL Fall Star Game
item.description: SURPRISE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 14: Ike Irish #10 of the Baltimore Orioles stands on deck during a game between the Peoria Javelinas and Surprise Saguaros at Surprise Stadium on October 14, 2026 in Surprise, Arizona. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Monday, Camden Chatters! I hope you enjoyed this lovely fall weekend. After a brief flurry of activity around the first of the month, things have gone quiet around MLB. Despite the short timeline due to the impending owners’ lockout, not much has taken place. No notable free agent signings have occurred, no interesting trades have gone down. We’re less than a month from baseball shutting down, so these teams better get hopping! Maybe we will see some action this week, as the General Manager meetings kick off in Las Vegas tomorrow. The GM meetings are usually about laying the groundwork for off-season deals, but the tone could be different this year due to the unusual circumstances. At least, I hope it will be different. We’re looking at a bleak winter for baseball, so I’d like to have some things take place in the next week or so. I would recommend the Orioles sign Trevor Rogers to a contract, if they’re looking for my advice. While we wait on the Orioles and the rest of the league to start doing things, we can focus on the baseball that is happening now. Namely, the Arizona Fall League. Last night, the Fall Start Game took place as the AFL winds down for the season. Four Orioles prospects were selected to represent the AL: pitchers Braxton Bragg and Patrick Reilly, and outfielders Vance Honeycutt and Ike Irish. I can’t tell you who won the game. It was tied 3-3 in the seventh inning when I turned in for the night. But I can tell you how our prospects did, and that’s all the really matters. Reilly started the game for the AL team, and it did not go well. He didn’t allow a hit, which is great! But he walked three batters and allowed a run to score on a wild pitch. Not what you want to see from the starting pitcher. Bragg pitched the third, and fared better. He struck out the first two batters, one called and one swinging. Then he induced a groundout to end the inning. Honeycutt, who has had an outstanding fall season, went 0-for-2 with two strikeouts. He did take a walk. Irish had a more successful night. He singled in a run in the third inning, which at the time gave the AL a 2-1 lead. He also walked. The Fall Star game is at weird time in the schedule. The AFL is off today, then has two more days of “regular season” games. Thursday through Saturday is a quick playoff round, with the championship taking place on Saturday night. The Peoria Javelinas, which is home to the Orioles’ prospects, are currently tied for first place at 16-10. item.title: Jim Harbaugh is a clown and the Chargers are his circus
item.description: There were 13 minutes remaining in the third quarter when it became clear that Jim Harbaugh checked out. Houston was up 24-9, Tre Harris had just been hurt, adding another injury on offense the Chargers couldn’t endure. Harbz marched along the sideline pre-snap, not watching the next run play, looking like a man who just wanted to keep walking, out of the tunnel, and out of Los Angeles altogether. Perhaps he should. The woes the Chargers have faced this season aren’t entirely of Harbaugh’s creation, but his staggering inability to make changes, or accept what’s best for the team’s future — those are on his shoulders. Harbaugh made headlines prior to Sunday for infamously, nonsensically remaining insistent that the Chargers won’t be trading players away at the deadline because it sends “the message of giving up on the season.” News flash: The Chargers are 0-8 right now. They are dead last in the AFC West, the AFC as a conference, and the NFL as a whole. They are the worst team in football by a country mile, and while Harbz might not like the message they’re “giving up on the season,” they need to give up on the season, because at this point the Chargers are facing another rebuild. It’s impossible to calculate everything wrong for the this season. Injuries wrecked the offensive line, and that started some dominoes falling. The defense is doing its best despite being an afterthought, and while they’re not good by any stretch of the imagination, I hesitate to lump them in with the team’s issues as a whole — because at least they’re performing the basic elements of the job. Offensively, this team has become a dumpster fire. I don’t know the last time a player fell off the map the way that Justin Herbert has this season. Watching him play against the Texans was painful, because it’s as if he’s forgotten how to make the simplest of throws and is consistently trying to generate explosive plays, regardless of whether they’re good or not. This results in all of his best traits: decision-making and processing fly out the window, turning him into a one-dimensional JUGS machine that doesn’t care who catches the ball. More often than not it’s been the opponents, as Herbert moved to 11 interceptions on the season and only six touchdowns. We’ve lost the version of fiery Harbaugh who will do anything to win. That guy would bench players on principle when they weren’t doing their jobs. He would chew out his assistants, demanding something improve. Now he’s in this mode of performative competitiveness, doing dumb things like going for two while down 38-15 in the fourth quarter to show that he hasn’t quit — despite doing everything else to indicate that he has. This is a coach whose heart just isn’t in it. He made the switch to the NFL to avoid the fallout from the Michigan investigation into Connor Stallions, not because he really wanted to be a professional football coach again. item.title: Inter and inspiresport renew their Partnership
item.description: Inter and inspiresport renew their Partnership FC Internazionale Milano is delighted to announce the extension of the Partnership with inspiresport , building on years of collaboration that have brought thousands of young players closer to the club through unforgettable football tours. A new chapter in a journey built on shared values and lasting impact. On Monday 9th November at Inter HQ, an Inter delegation welcomed Steve Butchart, Managing Director at inspiresport , to celebrate the renewal of a partnership that continues to inspire and connect young football enthusiasts with the world of Inter. The renewed agreement extends the Inter Academy Experience programme through 2031, reinforcing a successful collaboration that began in 2018 and brings more than 700 boys and girls from the UK, USA and Australia to Milano each year. The partnership looks ahead to many more years of unforgettable experiences for the next generation of football fans.

item.title: ‘We call him…’: Bones Hyland says T-Wolves have a new nickname for Joan Beringer after his 'broken nose'
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves made it four wins in a row after beating the Utah Jazz 115-100. LaMelo Ball stole the show as he always does, while Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points. But the bench more than played its part, especially Bones Hyland and Joan Beringer. The former has a nickname for the Frenchman now. Bones Hyland says Joan Beringer is called ‘The Batman’ and shares a ‘funny story’ Beringer suffered a nasal fracture during the Minnesota Timberwolves’ win over the New Orleans Pelicans in the NBA Cup. The Frenchman suffered an inadvertent elbow to his face. He still scored two free throws with blood coming out of his nose, but he didn’t return after being diagnosed with a fracture. There were fears that Beringer would be sidelined, but the teenager played against the Jazz on Sunday night while wearing a protective mask. Hyland claimed that Beringer even wore the mask in the locker room when he first got it, thus leading to a new nickname. He said: “We call him ‘The Batman’. It’s a funny story. We were in the locker room, and he had that mask on. They told him he had to wear it. He ain’t take it off in the locker room. “I was like: ‘Joan, you ain’t even on the court right now. You can take your mask off’. But that was the first time he was wearing the mask with a broken nose. “But he’s a warrior, bro. We love Joan. He has come in with young legs and runs the floor for us, blocks shots, and makes shots go left or right. We love Joan!” ‘The Batman’ is a really cool nickname for Beringer, but what’s better is his performances for the Minnesota Timberwolves this season. The teenager has impressed everyone and has earned a lot of praise, including one from his country’s biggest basketball star, Victor Wembanyama. Beringer is not a starter yet, but if he keeps developing at the same rate, he will become a star in the not-too-distant future. item.title: 2026 MVBrewers #1: William Contreras
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: William Contreras #24 of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts after hitting an RBI Double during the sixth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re kicking off our 2026 MVBrewers rankings, and the voting for this year’s No. 1 player was perhaps the closest we’ve ever seen: With 74 total votes in our poll on The Feed, catcher William Contreras edged second baseman Brice Turang with 37.9% of the vote (28 votes) compared to 35.1% (26 votes). Jacob Misiorowski garnered 18.9% (14 votes), while Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers, and write-in candidate Aaron Ashby each picked up two votes (shoutout to @Berhaltersburner for the recognition). While Turang is a top-three MVP finisher in the league (likely behind Pete Crow-Armstrong and Shohei Ohtani), that’s a regular-season-only award, whereas we don’t have those restrictions here, and perhaps that’s exactly what separates Contreras from Turang. While Contreras ranked seventh on the team in bWAR (2.9) and sixth in fWAR (3.0), he added more immeasurable value than any other player, managing one of baseball’s pitching staffs. He also was an incredible ABS-challenger in the postseason — after an MLB-leading 195 challenges in the regular season at a 56.9% overturn rate, Contreras went 22/33 as a catcher in the postseason, including an incredible 10/13 in the World Series. Contreras also raked all postseason, slashing .373/.448/.588 with three homers, two doubles, nine RBIs, seven runs scored, and a steal across 13 games. And while Contreras had a great postseason, he had nothing to be ashamed of in the regular season. Yes, he turned in just 2.9 bWAR after eclipsing 3.7 WAR in each of his first three seasons with Milwaukee, but he still hit .270/.341/.417 with 18 homers, 27 doubles, 94 RBIs, and 82 runs. Part of the reason his WAR is deflated is a rough stretch from early July to mid-August — across 31 games, he went just 16-for-113, slashing .142/.240/.257 with two homers (one of which was a walk-off homer against the Marlins), five doubles, eight RBIs, and 10 runs scored. Not ideal for an All-MLB catcher. Even so, Contreras’ Baseball Savant page still features a lot of above-average metrics. He ranked in the top-third of the league in xwOBA (.334), xBA (.261), xSLG (.441), average exit velocity (90.3 mph), hard-hit rate (44.1%), squared-up rate (31.5%), whiff rate (20.7%), and strikeout rate (14.7%). He was also one of the league’s best catchers at catching base stealers, ranking in the 92nd percentile in caught stealing. Overall, it was a great season for Milwaukee’s backstop, and he’ll look to build on his strong postseason in the final year of his contract in 2027 ( or will the Brewers give him an extension? ). We’ll continue these rankings on Thursday with our No. 2 player. To weigh in on the voting, visit The Feed (the poll will

item.title: Chicago Cubs history unpacked — November 9
item.description: Free of charge for the discerning reader. Happy birthday to Tony Barnette*, and a mighty host of others. Today in baseball history, in 1976 – The Oakland Athletics give future Hall of Famer Billy Williams his unconditional release , ending his 18-year major league career. Williams, who spent all but two seasons with the Chicago Cubs , retires with 426 home runs, 1,475 RBI, 2,711 hits, and a .290 batting average, and other stories as well. Today in baseball history : 1912 – Frank Chance is sold by the Chicago Cubs to the Cincinnati Reds . When all National League clubs waive claims to him in December, the Reds free Chance to manage the Yankees . 1935 – Pitcher Bob Gibson is born in Omaha, Nebraska . Gibson will make his major league debut in 1959 , marking the start of a 17-year career with the St. Louis Cardinals and an election to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1981 . 1937 – St. Louis Cardinals Triple Crown winner Joe Medwick is named National League Most Valuable Player by the Baseball Writers Association of America . 1950 – The BBWAA name Sam Jethroe of the Boston Braves as the National League Rookie of the Year . At 31 years, 2 months, 18 days of age, Jethroe becomes the oldest rookie to win the award. He has been one of the best Negro Leagues players of his time. 1950 – After twenty-one years with the club, shortstop and future Hall of Famer Luke Appling is released by the Chicago White Sox allowing him to become the manager of the Memphis Chicks of the South Atlantic League . 1960 – In an extremely close vote (225 points to 222), Roger Maris beats Yankees teammate Mickey Mantle for the AL MVP Award . 1982 – Robin Yount , who hit .331 for the Milwaukee Brewers and led the American League in hits (210), doubles (46), and slugging percentage (.578), is a unanimous choice as AL Most Valuable Player . The future Hall of Famer captures all 27 first-place votes easily beating runner-ups Eddie Murray and Doug DeCinces . 1998 – Hall of Fame pitcher Jim “Catfish” Hunter announces that he is suffering from Lou Gehrig ‘s disease. The fatal disease, known medically as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, attacks the nerves in the spinal cord and the brain and leads to a loss of motor skills. Hunter will succumb to the disease less than a year later. 1999 – Kansas City Royals outfielder Carlos Beltran is named the American League Rookie of the Year . Beltran became the first rookie with 100 or more RBI since Mike Piazza had 112 in 1993 and the first in the AL since Mark McGwire had 118 in 1987 . Beltran is also the first rookie with a 100 run -100 RBI season since Fred Lynn in 1975 . 2010 – The winners of the 2010 American League Gold Glove Awards are announced. Mariners OF Ichiro Suzuki wins his tenth Gold Glove in as many years, tying Al Kaline and Ken Griffey Jr. for the most Gold Gloves by an AL flyhawk. 2020 – Kyle Lewis of the Mariners is the unanimous winner of the 2020 American League Rookie of the Year Award , while, in a sign of how the game has evolve

item.title: Drake Maye reverts to early-season self in loss to Packers
item.description: Drake Maye was announced as AFC Offensive Player of October last Wednesday, an honor reflective of his impressive turnaround. After struggling mightily over the first three weeks of the season, the New England Patriots quarterback rebounded nicely to take home the accolade. Four days later, the very same early-season Drake Maye made his return. He helped set the stage for the Patriots getting blown out at the hands of the Green Bay Packers. Maye turned the ball over three times during the 45-27 defeat , tossing a trio of interceptions in the first half that contributed to his team finding itself in an early hole it failed to get out of. And while the second-year passer did have some promising moments as well, those were once again overshadowed by his ball-security concerns. “We haven’t had a clean, a turnover-free game yet. It’s starting with me,” Maye said during his post-game presser at Gillette Stadium. “It’s one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games. I put our defense in a bad spot on the first drive, just gave them the football, had some other chances down the field, and have to see in front.” Sunday’s loss to the Packers was Maye’s second three-interception game of the season, making him the only player in the league with multiple such games on his record. On the year, Maye has now thrown 11 picks — tied with the Chargers’ Justin Herbert for most in the NFL. The first of his picks versus Green Bay already set the tone for the rest of the day. On his first pass attempt, Maye maneuvered a muddy pocket and lifted a floater across the body intended for wide receiver Mack Hollins. Instead of hitting his target, however, the ball landed in the waiting arms of safety Xavier McKinney. McKinney returned the interception 36 yards to set his offense up at the New England 9. Two players later the Packers took a 7-0 lead that continued to grow with the offense unable to find its rhythm. Even when it did, Maye’s interceptions quickly halted any progress. He threw a second pick early in the second period, on a play reminiscent of his first interception of the year. Just like in Week 1, when he was targeting Romeo Doubs deep down the left sideline, he attempted to connect with Kyle Williams only to see the pass broken up and intercepted on the deflection. Two possessions later, after the Patriots had decreased their deficit to 17-7 with a 30-yard touchdown pass from Maye to Rhamondre Stevenson, McKinney registered another pick when he undercut a throw intended for Eli Raridon. “Just throwing the football in spots that I don’t think I should have thrown it,” said Maye about his three INTs. “The first one, I think I just got to see the guys deep, see the safety positions. The second one happens, maybe throw it a little farther. And the third one, they’re jumping cross routes, so I got to see in front.” Besides preventing three Patriots scoring opportunities, the interceptions also directly set up two Packers touchdowns. item.title: Here’s how to watch Bills at Vikings in Week 8
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 13: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills attempts a pass during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2022 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s finally Monday, which means the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings finally square off under the brightest football lights of Monday Night Football to close out Week 9 of NFL action. Buffalo and Minnesota share more than a few similarities as two smaller-market teams that have yet to win a Super Bowl despite each franchise having had four tries at the Lombardi Trophy. Bills Mafia and the SKOL Family hope this season is different with both teams entering tonight’s game at 6-1. Yet, the circumstances in both getting to this point are far different. It’s Buffalo’s top-scoring offense (33.3 ppg) against Minnesota’s top-ranked, stingy scoring defense (13.3 ppg allowed). The Bills have struggled on defense a fair bit this season, while the Vikings have problems of their own on offense. Now, Minnesota turns to quarterback Carson Wentz again because starting quarterback Kyler Murray deals with a hamstring injury that has him listed as week-to-week. The Bills and Vikings have played just 15 times dating back to their first matchup in October 1971. Minnesota leads the all-time series 9-6, having won the last game between the two franchises. That 33-30 overtime loss for Buffalo came in Orchard Park, NY back in November 2022. Josh Allen is 1-1 against the Vikings since entering the NFL, with his first professional win coming in a 27-6 victory back in September of his rookie season in 2018. That game is now part of Bills lore, thanks to Allen’s hurdle of linebacker Anthony Barr. item.title: Puka Nacua injury: Rams WR hurts knee vs. Commanders
item.description: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Puka Nacua had a monster game for the Los Angeles Rams during Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The wide receiver hauled in 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, and added another 20 yards on a pair of rushing attempts, as the Rams moved above .500 on the season. But now Los Angeles is holding its collective breath, as Nacua is set for an MRI after injuring his knee on the Rams’ final offensive play of the game. According to Adam Schefter of ESPN, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to “determine the extent of the injury.” Schefter and Mike Garafolo are reporting that the team “does not elieve he suffered a torn ACL,” but that the “imaging Monday will tell more.” You can see that final offensive snap here: All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 The play was on of Nacua’s two rushing attempts on the game, an end-around design that was held to a short gain. Nacua did get up right after the tackle, but walked back to the sideline rather gingerly. Los Angeles plays the Arizona Cardinals in Week 10, before a bye week in Week 11. Their next game is the new “Thanksgiving Eve” contest on Wednesday, November 25 against the Green Bay Packers. Note: This is a developing story and will be updated.

item.title: Nick Wright calls Patrick Mahomes a ‘cyborg’ after getting injured with hit during Chiefs win over Jets
item.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes pushed through a serious hit in their 35-12 win over the New York Jets. Mahomes did not miss a single offensive snap in the win, going 23/31 on pass attempts for 242 yards, two TDs, and a 117.9 passer rating. He also rushed for eight yards on two carries in a strong performance. Mahomes was tackled by Jets EDGE David Bailey in the second quarter and appeared to suffer an elbow injury, but his resolute toughness made him push through the discomfort and finish the win after avoiding major injury. Patrick Mahomes hailed as a cyborg by Nick Wright Watching Mahomes take that rough hit and escape without injury left FOX Sports’ Nick Wright in awe of the 33-year-old QB. “Also… Never a doubt. Mahomes is a cyborg. 99% of QBs have their elbow dislocated on that hit. He missed zero snaps. They’ll be 8-2 heading into Buffalo.” It’s since been confirmed that Mahomes’ injury is an elbow strain/sprain after post-game MRIs, with the QB likely not missing their game against the Atlanta Falcons on November 15. Mahomes admitted after the win that the hit from Bailey had a major impact on his performance, as he struggled to throw the ball as deep and precisely as he normally can. Nonetheless, even a slightly wounded Mahomes would be a better option than backup QB Justin Fields for the Chiefs right now, especially as they look to challenge the 7-2 Denver Broncos for THE top spot in the AFC West. While Mahomes has not been among the MVP contenders this season, he has had a strong comeback season after rushing through recovery from a torn ACL. Over the season, Mahomes has thrown 177/263 for 2,037 yards, 14 TDs, and four INTs for a 101.8 passer rating. Avoiding a season-ending elbow injury on that play was a moment of good fortune for the Chiefs, and the franchise will hope that fortune pushes them through till the end of the season. item.title: AI echo chambers and sanity in tech leadership: Three case studies
item.description: "AI delusion" remains loosely defined, but most of us know it when we see it: exaggerated faith in the technology's power, applicability, or nature, coupled with a refusal to acknowledge its limitations. It's bad in the individual, as when an elderly relative emails you a hallucination-laden ChatGPT summary. It's worse in management, when your boss insists that AI slop is genius marketing content at a bargain rate. It is terrifying in tech CEOs. It is not, thankfully, compulsory. Consider three recent examples of technology leadership in the age of AI. One would be Pythonesque were the disconnect with engineers and the public not so profound. Another risks becoming a business-school case study in how to demolish customer trust. The third offers something less fashionable: robust pragmatism. Saving the best till last, y'all. Case 1: we present for your consideration Sam Altman of OpenAI, one of the few actually at the controls of the singularity machine. It seems churlish to pluck just one luscious fruit out of that cornucopia of choices, yet we must. Sam Altman thinks it is a sin against the natural order that so much RAM is idling in machines owned by individuals, organizations, and anywhere that isn't Big AI . It's oh so inefficient. How convenient that the efficient allocation of scarce resources should favor the business he runs. Free market schmarket. Altman has since said his remarks were taken out of context and that he wants consumers to have as much memory as they like. The efficiency argument still reveals whose priorities come first. This is the best kind of delusion, one with an undeniable truth at its core – memory does indeed get used far more intensively in AI model makers and inference servers than in your laptop. For a business selling the future, treating privately owned hardware as an inefficient allocation of resources has a distinctly Soviet flavor, and the American right has vowed to stamp out socialist extremism. Get on with it, chaps, you've only got two years left . That Altman can't see this is the best bit of the misconception. There are two potential root causes of this Marxist-Leninist-Altmanism. One is that he's mathed the math and worked out that the only way OpenAI can hit the numbers is if it gets every last byte in the world, hot off the fab. The other is that you can't run on-prem on an 8 GB state-mandated Chromebook, and on-prem is otherwise going to twist his melon until it falls off. Case 2: Andy Yen, CEO of Proton, the company behind Proton Mail and Proton VPN. You, me, and the household cat know ProtonMail as the secondary email that's worth paying for. You want the best recovery backup email for Gmail, you want it as an accessible end-to-end encrypted email service. You want it because it is all about stable spotless security, all about the end users, all about being there when you absolutely need it. It is safe to recommend, and you do. Or rather that's what you thought about ProtonMail et al until the sa

item.title: Week 10 fantasy football PPR rankings: Allen, Walker III, Smith-Njigba lead
item.description: Josh Allen , Kenneth Walker III and Jaxon Smith-Njigba lead my Week 10 fantasy football PPR rankings, with the Chiefs running back coming off a three-touchdown game against the Jets heading into Sunday’s trip to Atlanta. Walker ran for 102 yards and a score and added two touchdown catches in a 35-12 win. Smith-Njigba became the NFL’s first 1,000-yard receiver Sunday and now faces a Raiders defense allowing 28.7 half-PPR points per game to receivers . These rankings are an early rough draft. Monday night’s Bills-Vikings game hasn’t been played, and the trade deadline arrives Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. Just remember players listed here aren’t guaranteed to play, and I’ll update the rankings before Thursday’s Commanders-Giants game and again before Sunday’s early kickoff in Munich. The full positional rankings tables are at the end of the article. That takes Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, Eagles running back Saquon Barkley and Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving out of the mix. item.title: DisCos Apologise To Nigerians Over Power Outages
item.description: Electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) have apologised to Nigerians over persistent electricity shortages across the country, acknowledging the hardship caused by weeks of prolonged blackouts. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan, tendered the apology on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . “I’d like to first of all start by apologising to Nigerians. Apology is needed; it is essential because Nigerians have been taken through this problem over the past few weeks,” he said. Oduntan also criticised what he described as a return to the blame game among operators in the electricity sector, recalling that similar disagreements between stakeholders had characterised the industry between 2016 and 2019. He said distribution companies, transmission operators, generation companies and gas suppliers had previously blamed one another for poor electricity supply instead of addressing the underlying problems. “Our major problem is that we have started that very wrong route that we went through between 2016 and 2019. What is that? Blame game. “Part of what happened at that time is that people will blame the DisCos, DisCos will blame TCN, TCN will blame GenCos, GenCos will blame the gas suppliers, and gas suppliers will blame payment issues. We have returned to that, and I think there is a need to arrest that,” he said. Oduntan Questions Conflicting Explanations A combo of the Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors (ANED), Sunday Oduntan and electricity installations. The ANED spokesperson also expressed concern over statements issued by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) regarding the factors responsible for the electricity shortages. He said NISO had attributed the supply challenges partly to low water levels and inadequate gas supply, while the NNPC subsequently issued a statement indicating that gas was available. Oduntan, however, questioned the information provided by the national oil company, insisting that it should clarify whether outstanding payments were affecting gas supply to power generation companies. “From the NNPC statement, it is very clear that they came to tell us half-truths. What I would have expected NNPC to do is to go ahead and talk to us whether there are payment issues. We need to know whether gas was paid for and delivered, who did, who didn’t,” he said. The ANED CEO urged the Minister of Power to intervene by bringing the relevant stakeholders together to establish the actual causes of the shortages. “This back and forth blame game between gas suppliers, NNPC and, of course, TCN or NISO, I think the Minister of Power needs to take charge. There is a need for this leadership because, at the end of the day, they need to call them together,” he said. Prolonged Blackouts The apology comes amid growing fr

item.title: Three-time Olympic judo champion announces bid for French presidency
item.description: Three-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner is to run for the French presidency, with his campaign intending to “show that we can turn France around”. The 37-year-old said he would not run on a left- or right-wing ticket but instead focus his campaign on “bringing the French people together”, with the slogan for his campaign “The France we want”. He told French outlet Le Parisien on Monday: “France is a great country. It has allowed me to become the person I am today and has given me the opportunity to dream big. “Today, that’s what’s missing. That ambition is gone; that hope is gone. “I see a divide in society across the country, but I do not accept what I hear in the mouths of young people, that it is difficult today to imagine a future. That is why I decided to commit myself, alongside the French people, and to become a candidate for the presidency.” An election to decide Emmanuel Macron’s successor is to be held in April next year; Macron, having served two consecutive terms, is ineligible to run again. Riner has no experience of politics but is a well-known and popular figure in France, and has previously hinted at a desire to enter politics at the highest level. He said in an interview last year: “I am a citizen above all, not just a sportsperson. If tomorrow I enter politics, it wouldn’t be to be a minister, it would be to change things. The best role would be president.” Riner, who was born in Guadeloupe, grew up in Paris. He is a nine-time heavyweight world champion, two-time openweight world champion, and has two Olympic bronze medals to go with his three individual golds and two mixed team gold medals. He was a torchbearer during the Olympic torch relay ahead of the 2024 Games in Paris, and lit the cauldron during the opening ceremony alongside retired sprinter Marie-Jose Perec. Riner said that the experience of the home Olympic Games uniting the country inspired him to enter politics, saying: “I saw a whole country come together, proud, happy. I thought to myself, what we have been able to do for 15 days, we must be able to do for the country.” He said his decision to run for president would not end his judo career or hopes of competing at the LA Games 2028.

item.title: Celtics' First 10 Games Reveal An Unexpected Statistical Strength
item.description: Celtics' First 10 Games Reveal An Unexpected Statistical Strength originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics have completed their first 10 games of the 2026-27 season, and their early record provides plenty of reasons for optimism. Boston improved to 8-2 with Sunday's 117-97 win over the Milwaukee Bucks, extending its winning streak to three games. The Celtics have shown offensive versatility, defensive improvement and an ability to win games in different ways. However, one statistic stands out as particularly encouraging through the opening stretch. Boston has outscored its opponents by 107 points over its first 10 contests, an average advantage of 10.7 points per game. Scoring Margin Tells An Important Story The Celtics have scored 1,150 points through 10 games, averaging exactly 115.0 per game. Their opponents have scored 1,043 points, an average of 104.3. 8-2 in our first 10 games ✅ https://t.co/EyhGK6LCk9 — Boston Celtics (@celtics) November 9, 2026 That differential shows that Boston's success has involved more than simply winning close games. The Celtics have delivered several convincing performances, including a 134-99 victory over Chicago and a 119-80 win against Charlotte. Those results helped build a substantial scoring advantage even with two defeats on the schedule. Boston Has Several Ways To Win Jayson Tatum remains an important offensive centerpiece, but the Celtics have received significant contributions from other players. Paul George scored 27 points in Sunday's victory over Milwaukee, while Tatum added 21. Payton Pritchard has also produced several strong scoring performances, helping Boston maintain offensive production when opponents focus on its biggest stars. The Celtics have shown an ability to generate points from the perimeter while also receiving contributions inside. MORE: The Celtics Shook Off a Slow Start and Took Control in Milwaukee Defense Has Supported The Offense Boston's early success is not solely a product of scoring. The Celtics have held opponents below 100 points in four of their first 10 games, including victories over Chicago, Orlando, Charlotte and Milwaukee. That defensive consistency has allowed Boston to control games even when its offense experiences slower stretches. The team also has responded effectively to adversity, winning three consecutive contests after its November 2 loss to Houston. An 8-2 record is an encouraging beginning, but the scoring margin suggests something more significant. The Celtics have not merely survived their first 10 games. They have frequently controlled them. item.title: F1 standings 2026: Driver and constructor points, results for Formula One season
item.description: F1 standings 2026: Driver and constructor points, results for Formula One season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 Formula 1 season started at Melbourne Park with the Australian Grand Prix on the weekend of March 6-8. Lando Norris became world champion for the first time in 2025 after finishing third at a dramatic concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, edging out race winner Max Verstappen in the title battle by just two points. Oscar Piastri finished third. It ended Verstappen's streak of four consecutive world titles and gave McLaren their first since Lewis Hamilton in 2008. McLaren also claimed the constructors' title after a largely dominant 2025, with Mercedes finishing a distant second. The possibility of this being the start of a dominant period for McLaren — similar to those enjoyed by Red Bull and Mercedes in recent years — was complicated by a series of new regulations affecting engines, chassis, tyres, and fuel. Kimi Antonelli made light of predictions that the opening weeks of the season would be wide open as he reeled off five consecutive wins, following Mercedes teammate George Russell's triumph in Australia. Since then, Ferrari duo Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have each stood on the top step of the podium. Antonelli increased his advantage at the top of the table with victory in the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa, before Norris belatedly claimed the first win of his title defence in Hungary and followed that with victory in the Netherlands. Antonelli then produced arguably the drive of the year to win in Italy after beginning in 19th place on the grid. He followed this by winning the inaugural Madrid grand prix ahead of Verstappen, but teammate Russell took the win in Azerbaijan. Verstappen triumphed in Sepang to keep up his pursuit of at least a top-three finish in the standings. Antonelli triumphed in the USA to now put himself within touching distance of becoming the world champion. item.title: Troops kill suspect, recover AK-47 in old Oyo park
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation IGBO DANU II, under the 2 Division of the Nigerian Army, have neutralised a suspected criminal and recovered an AK-47 rifle and other weapons during an operation in the Old Oyo National Park. The operation, conducted in collaboration with hybrid forces, also led to the destruction of temporary shelters suspected to have been used as hideouts by criminal elements operating in the forest. The Nigerian Army disclosed this in a statement, saying the encounter occurred on November 7, 2026, when troops conducting operations within the park engaged suspected criminals who fled upon sighting the advancing forces. The statement said the troops subsequently recovered an AK-47 rifle, one empty magazine and a Dane gun from the area. It added that during a follow-up operation on November 8, troops discovered the corpse of one of the fleeing suspects, confirming that one criminal element had been neutralised. According to the Army, the destruction of the temporary shelters was aimed at disrupting criminal activities and denying the suspects safe havens within the forested area. It said troops, in collaboration with other security stakeholders, remained committed to sustaining operations to dismantle criminal networks, deny them operational bases and restore security across the 2 Division Area of Responsibility. The Army added that exploitation of the general area was ongoing to track fleeing suspects and prevent them from regrouping.
