item.title: Portsmouth 1-2 Stoke City - fans' verdict
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Stoke City came from behind to win at Portsmouth and briefly go top of the Championship on Saturday. Here are some of your comments: Stoke City fans Phil: Even when we were up against it in the first half I was confident that we would get a goal back and go on from there to wrest control of the game. That result and how it happened speaks volumes for this new look Stoke team. Last season we'd have lost that. Their inner confidence filters through to the fans. There's a whole new vibe about SCFC this season. David : A poor first half, followed by a brave second when three substitutions by Mark Robins changed the balance of the side. Ben Wilmot has the happy knack of popping up with late winners and Stoke were deserved winners. A proper team, this Stoke. Liam : A tight championship game. We were miles off it in the first half but better in the second. We need to keep and use the ball better. However, the togetherness and resilience in this team is its super strength. Andrew : Great away win again, what a following from the Red Army, 7am on coach well worth it. Must say Pompey have also got good support and nice to hear home fans making some noise, Get a good striker in January, we could do it this year. Chris : Terrible first half performance from Stoke but realised that Pompey were already playing at their maximum, while Stoke had another few gears. Stoke controlled the second half and there was only going to be one winner. Great set of results the last few weeks - shame the international break will ruin the run!

item.title: MMQB – Turtling Up
item.description: Tell me if you’ve heard this one before during this season: Penn State races out to a big first half lead against an opponent that appears to be hapless, the coaches go into ultra conservative run-out-the-clock mode way too early in the game, and the previously hapless opponent comes roaring back. In the case of the earlier game against Wisconsin, the Lions built a 17-0 first half lead before going conservative, which ultimately bit the team in the ass as the Badgers compiled enough big plays down the stretch to beat the Lions 24-20. In the case of this weekend’s game against Washington, Penn State built a 28-6 halftime lead before going conservative, and the team did just enough to eke out a 28-25 win. Someone needs to have a word with Matt Campbell about not turtling up when he has a lead. Admittedly he is known as a conservative coach, but that’s twice in the same season that he went conservative in the first half of a conference game expecting to just run the clock out for 30+ minutes. I’m not sure what would work in the Big 12, but it sure as hell doesn’t work in the Big Ten. There are play calls that exist that both run the clock but also keep your offense – which was HUMMING in the first half – on the move. It’s not at all necessary to attempt to “kneel out the clock” for two full quarters of the game in all but name via three straight runs up the gut followed by a punt. Some of it is execution, to be fair. This Penn State team seems to have some sort of mental stigma about playing with a lead. They almost don’t believe that they can keep the good juju going, and are all collectively waiting for something to go bad. To hell with that. You’re good enough, obviously, as you built this lead by playing your game in the first half. Keep it up and you dogwalk your opponent. While execution is certainly something to keep an eye on, even that comes from the coaching. This staff needs to trust in themselves and their players and just keep playing like they did to get things going. Who knows if this issue will pop up again this season. Even if it did, at this point I don’t know that Campbell and Co. would do anything different than they’ve been doing. But Matt Campbell is going to need to have a long look in the mirror about just exactly how he expects his Penn State teams going forward to compete in this conference with that sort of mentality. Show some toughness, show some grit, show some belief in your players and coaches, and just go out and play your game. But hey. A win is a win, right?

item.title: Alexis Mac Allister urges Liverpool to maintain momentum after securing crucial win before international break
item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Alexis Mac Allister has called on his Liverpool team-mates to keep their foot on the gas after a vital Premier League victory. The Argentine midfielder played a starring role as the Reds moved into the international break on a high following their success at Selhurst Park. Mac Allister opens his account Liverpool headed into the international break in style, securing a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on Sunday. Mac Allister set the tone early on, breaking the deadlock with a clinical header. His contribution was followed by goals from Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, ensuring the three points stayed with the visitors despite a late consolation penalty from Eddie Nketiah. Reflecting on his first league goal of the campaign, Mac Allister expressed his delight at finding the net from a set-piece situation. "It feels good. It's the first one in the Premier League, but I scored twice in the Champions League and in another competition, so it's great to score, especially in a set-piece because it's something that I like. I think people and the coaching staff are realising I like it as well," the midfielder told BBC Sport , as quoted by the club's official website . The Argentine international also touched upon the technical improvements the squad has made, specifically regarding dead-ball scenarios. He admitted that the team had learned from recent defensive lapses. "We do work [on them] and we know how important it is. The other day we lost a game where we conceded three set-pieces. Today we won it because we scored from it so we understand how important it is, especially in football nowadays and the Premier League is becoming more and more physical," he added. Defensive resilience at Selhurst Park Winning away in South London is rarely an easy task, and Mac Allister was quick to credit the defensive unit for standing firm against a determined Palace side. While the scoreline suggested a comfortable win, the midfielder noted that the match was a significant test of their resolve. He singled out the central defenders for their ability to withstand pressure throughout the afternoon. "It was a difficult game. We know that when we come to Crystal Palace that it's always going to be a difficult game. They can play very good football but I think we defended the box quite well, especially our centre-backs, they were really, really good. But it was difficult. Sometimes we tried to press and it was not perfect, so they could come out from it and they created chances," Mac Allister explained. Alisson remains the difference maker A key factor in Liverpool's success was once again the presence of Alisson Becker between the posts. The Brazilian goalkeeper produced several top-class saves to keep the hosts at bay during crucial moments. item.title: ‘You just don’t know’: Patrick Mahomes reacts to ‘scary’ injury situation against Jets
item.description: Dec 7, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) lowers his head during the fourth quarter against the Houston Texans at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs picked up a dominant 35-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday, but they had a scary moment along the way as superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a big hit to his throwing arm in the second quarter. For a moment, it looked like he could be seriously hurt. Mahomes was able to stay in the game, and an MRI reportedly didn’t reveal any major injury. But after the game, the Chiefs star admitted that the moment scared him, especially after the knee injury that ended his season last year. Mahomes’ Injury Scare Late in the second quarter, Jets edge rusher David Bailey hit Mahomes’ right arm as he was throwing, with Will McDonald IV and Darrell Jackson Jr. also getting a piece of him on the play. Mahomes grimaced on the ground and then walked off slowly with his arm hanging at his side. But Mahomes flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw a few warm-up passes, and returned without missing a snap. Chiefs assistant athletic trainer Julie Frymyer worked on his arm at halftime, and head coach Andy Reid adjusted the game plan in the second half to lean on short throws. Mahomes finished 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both of which came before the hit. After the game, sources told ESPN’s Ian Rapoport that an MRI didn’t show any major injury to Mahomes’ right elbow. The Chiefs will monitor it for pain and swelling ahead of next Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons. ‘That stuff scares you’ Mahomes said after the game that he was always going to try to get back out there despite the injury. “If I’m able to play, I’m going to play,” Mahomes said, via ESPN’s Nate Taylor . “That’s part of the game. It scares you in moments, when you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn’t feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime.” He also admitted that the injury brought back memories of last season, when he tore his ACL and LCL in his left knee in December. “Any time it’s elbows and knees, it’s always scary, just because you just don’t know,” Mahomes said. “Even my knee last year, after we were doing the initial test, I thought, because I could walk off the field, I was going to be good. Then, all of a sudden, you do one test, and you’re just out [for the rest of the season]. That stuff scares you. Once I could throw the ball, I knew it wasn’t a ligament and it was more muscles.” Mahomes said he expects to be sore but believes he’ll be ready to go against Atlanta. “It’s definitely something that scares you more than anything,” he said. “I feel good now. item.title: Against All Odds: HomeWork Group, Africa Hands Over 14 Luxury Maisonettes at King’s Court, Ikeja GRA
item.description: GMD reaffirms commitment as firm records second project completion in 2026 HomeWork Group Africa has handed over 14 fully serviced three- and four-bedroom maisonettes at King’s Court, a residential development located on Adekunle Fajuyi Street, Ikeja GRA, Lagos. The handover ceremony, held on October 27, 2026, marked the completion of the project, which commenced in July 2021. King’s Court features spacious living areas and kitchens, private courtyards designed to promote cross-ventilation, large windows that allow natural lighting and deep balconies. The estate also provides power, water, security, CCTV, parking, a gym and a swimming pool. One of the homeowners commended the quality of the completed development and the consistent communication maintained by the company throughout the project. Speaking at the handover, the Group Managing Director of HomeWork Group Africa expressed gratitude for the completion and reaffirmed the company’s commitment to delivering quality homes. “ God establishes the works of our hands, and now we have the thrill of yet another completion. For us at HomeWork Group Africa, King’s Court is a story of determination. We promised our clients quality homes, and despite all odds, we have delivered.” King’s Court is the company’s second completed project in 2026, following the opening of Malvin Mall, a six-storey commercial development on Admiralty Way, Lekki, Lagos. HomeWork Group Africa is also preparing to hand over two residential developments before the end of the year. Yellowstone, located in Lekki Phase 1, comprises four terrace units and a penthouse, while Hines Court 2, situated on Freedom Way, Lekki, consists of 32 two- and three-bedroom flats. Founded in 2008, HomeWork Group Africa said it has completed more than 20 estate projects and delivered nearly 400 units. The company said the King’s Court handover further strengthens its portfolio of residential and commercial developments across Lagos. item.title: 2027: I’ve laid the foundation, my second term will be consolidation – Otti
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Chioma Otti, has said that the achievements recorded by his administration in the last three years represent only the foundation of his development agenda, assuring that the next four and a half years will focus on consolidating the gains and entrenching reforms across the state. Otti, who stated this during the South-East Conference of Dominion City Global, held in Aba, assured residents that his administration is committed to taking the state to the next level of development. Describing the achievements of his administration as a dress rehearsal, Otti said his government is determined to deepen ongoing reforms and deliver practical development outcomes that would have a lasting impact on the lives of the people. He said, “What has happened here is what I call a dress rehearsal, to let people know that they haven’t seen anything yet. What we have built in the last three years is just the foundation. “So, the next four and a half years, we will use them to consolidate. And when I say consolidation, I mean consolidation – changes that are irreversible. “My administration is not interested in making unrealistic promises but in implementing practical policies and projects capable of transforming the state.” He disclosed that his government is working towards ensuring a constant electricity supply across the state. According to him, the move would enable Abia to strengthen its electricity regulatory framework, support power generation and distribution capacity, and facilitate the distribution of excess electricity to other parts of the state. The governor also noted that his administration had instituted a monthly media chat to ensure that residents are adequately informed about government activities, policies and achievements. Otti reiterated his administration’s commitment to fairness, equity and merit in governance, declaring that there is no state-of-origin discrimination in Abia, as everyone living in the state is regarded as an Abian and treated equally. He charged Christians to demonstrate their faith through practical actions, adding that meaningful progress requires commitment, hard work and personal responsibility, as people should not expect miracles without making the necessary efforts. The governor congratulated the leadership of Dominion City Global on the conference and the construction of its massive facility in Aba, expressing admiration for the scale of the project and commending the church for its commitment to advancing the work of God. Earlier, the president of Dominion City Church, Pastor David Ogbueli, commended the governor for demonstrating servant leadership and transforming the state through purposeful governance. item.title: Portal breach at Germany's top university exposes every registered user's password
item.description: Attackers stole central university login passwords belonging to everyone registered with the Technical University of Munich's myTUM portal, including an admin whose credentials were then used to attack a second system. TUM restored access to its TUMonline campus management system on Monday morning, allowing users to change their passwords. The university disclosed the attack on November 6. The initial attack targeted the myTUM portal, which serves students and faculty members, providing centralized online access to services and documents. TUM said the attackers used the admin's credentials to launch a follow-on attack on TUMonline, its central campus management system, which forced the IT team to take it offline. The university has not disclosed how the attackers initially gained access or how the stolen passwords were stored. It did not immediately answer questions about the number of affected users. It also did not specify whether this sysadmin had multi-factor authentication (MFA) switched on, but it confirmed that "user accounts with MFA were protected from this attack." Attackers may also have accessed names, home addresses, and dates of birth. Potentially exposed employee records included work addresses and phone numbers, while student records included ID numbers, degree programs, and completed semesters. "The attackers' access within TUMonline was largely logged," said Dr Alexander Braun, CIO at TUM, in the disclosure. "After analyzing these logs, we currently assume that no other data from TUMonline was compromised, such as grades or college applications. We are continuing to investigate this." TUM is directing users to reset their passwords through Microsoft 365 where possible. Those without MFA already configured must instead use a German electronic ID or request a reset email while connected to the campus network. The university also warned users to watch for phishing and fraud, and to change any passwords reused elsewhere. TUM ranks first in Germany and 25th worldwide in the QS university rankings. The STEM-focused institution reports 51,954 students across its German campuses and TUM Asia in Singapore, plus 12,850 employees. ®

item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to conducting free, fair, transparent and peaceful elections, warning individuals and groups planning to instigate violence that they will be arrested and prosecuted. The State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr. Nawani Aboki, gave the assurance while addressing journalists, stakeholders, party supporters and government partners in Lafia on Monday. Aboki said the government was monitoring the security situation across the state’s local government areas to ensure that voters could exercise their franchise without fear or intimidation. Warning those contemplating violence, the commissioner said the government’s preference for peace should not be mistaken for weakness. “Quietness does not mean that somebody is weak. At times, when someone is pushed, the time comes when they must act. “Anyone who wants to perpetuate violence will be arrested and prosecuted to ensure we have peaceful elections,” he warned. He urged political parties and candidates to conduct their campaigns in an orderly and civilised manner, stressing that political violence would serve no useful purpose in the electoral process or the development of the state. On voter participation, Aboki urged eligible residents to ensure their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) were ready and safely kept ahead of the elections. He advised voters against waiting until election day to collect their PVCs and encouraged those yet to register to take advantage of the online voter registration platform. Highlighting infrastructure and social development projects undertaken by the Federal Government and the administration of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the commissioner cited the proposed transformation of the Federal Polytechnic, Nasarawa, into a specialised mining university, as well as the Leather Designing and Craft School in Doma. On infrastructure, he listed the ongoing federal government dualisation and expansion of the Nasarawa-Keffi road network and the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe Superhighway among projects expected to improve connectivity. In the health sector, Aboki said the upgrading and expansion of the Dalhatu Araf Specialist Hospital into the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, alongside facilities such as the Federal Eye Centre in Doma, had improved access to healthcare. The commissioner called on residents to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) gubernatorial candidate and other party candidates, arguing that such support would sustain the development initiatives of the Sule administration. “I know all of us are happy with the work Governor Sule has done. And so he has given us somebody we need to support. I want to call on all of us, and indeed the people of Nasarawa State, to support the candidate he has given us,” he said. item.title: Yobe enjoys relative peace across 17 LGAs – Buni
item.description: …Says farmers now have access to farmlands By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has said the state now enjoys relative peace across its 17 local government areas following years of insurgency, with farmers and business operators able to pursue their activities without major security disruptions. Buni spoke on Sunday night in Abuja at the Yobe Development and Partnership Roundtable, where he engaged distinguished indigenes of the state residing outside the state. He said the improved security situation had enabled farmers to return to their farmlands, while business owners could move freely across communities to conduct legitimate commercial activities. “Yobe State today enjoys relative peace across the 17 local government areas. Our farmers in the last few years have had access to their farmlands, while businessmen and women continue to traverse the length and breadth of the state conducting legitimate businesses peacefully,” the governor said. Recalling the difficult period of insurgency, Buni said the state had suffered widespread killings, displacement, destruction of communities and loss of livelihoods. “A few years back, our story was different, pathetic and despicable. Yobe, our dear state, the Pride of the Sahel, was plagued by a reckless, brutal and senseless insurgency security challenge. Many people were killed, others maimed, several communities displaced, and the surviving victims lost their means of livelihood,” he said. He, however, commended the resilience of the people, saying their determination to overcome the challenges had contributed to the state’s recovery. Buni acknowledged that rebuilding the state was difficult, considering the limited resources available to the government and the extensive destruction caused by insecurity. He said his administration supported economic recovery by distributing farm machinery and other agricultural inputs to farmers free of charge to improve productivity, strengthen food security and promote economic growth. According to him, the government also maintained minimal tax charges for businesses and other commercial activities to enable operators to recover from the effects of the insurgency. He said the administration deliberately refrained from reviewing existing tax rates, which he described as outdated and unrealistic. On education, Buni said his administration declared a state of emergency in the sector, particularly at the primary and basic levels, upon assuming office. He listed the achievements under the programme to include the reconstruction of 301 schools, construction of 929 new classrooms and rehabilitation of 748 others. The governor added that the government established 15 mega and model schools, as well as 10 new Government Girls Senior Secondary Schools, to promote girl-child education. item.title: Beyond the Asphalt: How Jetour’s High-Octane Lagos Convoy Brought Clean Water and Hope to Iwerekun Orile.
item.description: On Saturday, September 19, 2026, the roar of modern horsepower met the rhythm of drumming and celebration in Iwerekun Orile, Ibeju Lekki. Jetour Nigeria proved that the ultimate destination of any journey isn’t just where the road ends, it’s the lives transformed along the way. As part of the “2026 Jetour Africa Expedition: A Road Trip Beyond Limits,” a striking fleet featuring the Jetour Dashing, X50, X70 Plus, X90 Plus, T2, T2 PHEV, X70 PHEV, and the flagship G700, embarked on an ambitious test of endurance. Following a vital road safety briefing by the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Deputy Corps Commander Zonal Training Officer, Lagos, Mrs Esther Uzoma, and with seamless escort from the Nigeria Police Force and LASTMA, the convoy rolled out of Falomo Square, Ikoyi, turning heads across Victoria Island before pushing past the city’s glossy borders. Drivers and enthusiasts left the comfort of tarmac behind, putting the SUVs to the ultimate test across the unforgiving, swampy, and rock-strewn trails of the Coastal Highway. Yet, the real test of the day wasn’t mechanical resilience; it was human connection. The convoy’s final stop was the Roman Catholic Mission Primary School in Iwerekun Orile, where dust and exhaustion gave way to unbridled joy. There, Jetour officially commissioned a brand new, solar-powered borehole, delivering clean, reliable running water to a community that has spent generations yearning for it. The reception was deeply moving. School children broke into vibrant cultural dances, welcoming the convoy alongside elders, farmers, and market women. Beyond water, the team distributed food supplies to households, while pupils beamed with arms full of new books and refreshments. “This is where adventure meets purpose,” said Jetour Nigeria representative Kemi Adeola. “Our mission doesn’t stop at building capable vehicles; it lives in our pledge to drive tangible progress and touch the hearts of the communities we reach.” For the community, the impact was profound. High Chief Michael Oluwa hailed the water project as an unprecedented miracle in Iwerekun Orile’s history, pledging that the community would cherish and protect it. Equally overcome with emotion was the school’s head teacher, Mrs. Ariyike Bakre. “This is a special lifetime gift,” Bakre said, moved by the sight of water flowing on the school grounds. “It’s my first time seeing a solar-powered borehole. I am grateful to God for making this possible in my time, and for allowing our elders to witness this day. We cannot thank Jetour Nigeria enough, this water changes everything for our children and our people.” The day wound down at a tranquil beach lounge, where drivers and organizers gathered to celebrate the journey over good food, music, and shared memories. It was a fitting close to an unforgettable expedition: one that conquered demanding terrain, ignited the spirit of adventure, and left behind a lasting lifeline of clean water. item.title: Torrent underground
item.description: When Jane first heard about Memory and Imagination , a rare 1990s documentary about the Library of Congress, she was intrigued. But the Canadian writer in her 30s couldn’t find the movie anywhere — not on streaming services, not on YouTube, not on pirate sites — and her intrigue turned into obsession. Worried it might become a lost film , Jane decided to scour auction sites, search every library catalog she could think of, and even enlist some of her online acquaintances to find a copy. Her plan was to “share it with other people to help ensure it would be preserved into the future,” as she puts it. Jane knew the perfect tool for the task: a private torrent tracker. “I am ethically conflicted about piracy. I often feel guilty about it.” Private trackers are essentially the speakeasies of the online piracy world. Promoted primarily by word of mouth, they rely on secrecy, exclusivity, and strict community rules to shield everything that’s going on behind closed doors from the public’s prying eyes. What unites these communities is that they all use BitTorrent to trade media among like-minded file sharers. But their focuses range widely, from general-purpose trackers with catalogs so broad that they make Netflix look like a niche service to the many specialized communities for categories like Chinese movies, motorsports, visual effects tools, e-learning courses, and Japanese porn. There’s even a private tracker just for Frank Zappa music. Private trackers are known for massive and meticulously organized catalogs, which they owe to users like Jane, who, like every other pirate I talked to for this story, opted to be identified by a pseudonym due to the terabytes of copyrighted data they’ve been sharing. These are people willing to go the extra mile to find long-forgotten movies, rare concert recordings, or out-of-print books. “Many private tracker users are fully consumed with archive fever,” she says. At first, Jane had no luck finding a physical copy of that elusive documentary, which includes interviews with Steve Jobs and Julia Child. Nobody was selling it on eBay. Her local public library didn’t have it. Neither did any other public library in North America. And when she finally located a DVD that was available to the public, it was in the Bibliotheca Alexandrina — Egypt’s modern-day re-creation of the ancient library that’s long been synonymous with lost media. “That bowled me over,” Jane says. “This obscure movie I’m looking for is only available in the Library of Alexandria!” Eventually, Jane found Memory and Imagination for sale on a small online marketplace for historical media. Jane instantly bought a copy and uploaded it. “It looked like a digital rip of a severely degraded VHS tape,” she says. “I was still over the moon [that] I rescued this historically significant documentary.” Not everyone who uses private trackers shares Jane’s amateur-archivist zeal. Some are simply in it for easy access to pirated movies, TV shows, or other forms of

item.title: CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars
item.description: 6 Min Read CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Reflects After 378 Days on Simulated Mars The CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2 crew egress from their simulated Mars habitat, completing their mission on Oct. 31, 2026, at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credits: NASA/James Blair After 378 days without windows, the sounds of the outside world, or real-time calls with family and friends, four research volunteers stepped out of NASA’s Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, completing the agency’s second yearlong Mars surface simulation. Ross Elder, Ellen Ellis, James Spicer, and Matthew Montgomery entered the roughly 1,700-square-foot, 3D-printed habitat at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston on Oct. 19, 2025, for CHAPEA (Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog) Mission 2. The crew participated in simulated Marswalks, robotic operations, habitat maintenance, exercise, and crop cultivation. “Their work means more than completing a mission,” said Johnson Director Vanessa Wyche. “It is about preparing for the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth, gathering the knowledge we need to protect crew health and performance, and paving the way for future missions to the Moon and, one day, Mars.” Family, friends, and colleagues welcome the CHAPEA Mission 2 crew as they exit the building housing the Mars Dune Alpha habitat on Oct. 31, 2026. NASA/James Blair NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway put the crew’s time in isolation into perspective: While they were inside the habitat, he completed a 237-day mission aboard the space station and returned to Earth. During that same period, the Artemis II astronauts traveled around the Moon and set the record for the farthest humans have traveled from Earth. NASA also celebrated 25 years of continuous human presence aboard the International Space Station on Nov. 2, 2025. “The reality of what you guys did here required immense physiological and psychological strength, teamwork, and human grit,” Hathaway said. Supported by researchers and ground teams across the agency, the CHAPEA crew collected health and performance data while navigating limited resources and communication delays of up to 22 minutes each way. Ross Elder: Commander and Test Pilot Ross Elder, CHAPEA Mission 2 commander, prepares for a simulated Marswalk in the habitat’s airlock. Elder brought a U.S. Air Force experimental test pilot’s approach to leading the crew. He found simulated Marswalks and robotic exploration “uncannily similar” to operating as part of a flight. From inside the habitat, crew members remotely operated a drone and a rover to survey terrain and identify or collect rock samples. The demanding Marswalk schedule also sharpened his understanding of the physical preparation future explorers will need. Preparing suits, completing airlock procedures, and making long traverses took time and stamina. He emphasized nutrition, exercise, and rest as essential to sustaining that pace. item.title: Yes, it runs 'Doom': Satellite plays iconic game in world's 1st demonstration of orbital voice control
item.description: null A satellite went knee-deep in the dead, after a voice command from the ground activated the Doom video game in space. Playing a first-person shooter from 1993 was obviously not in the design plan for the PRETTY cubesat , which is run by a consortium including the European Space Agency (ESA). But the pioneering voice command opens up new worlds for satellite work, the team says. "Someone in distress at sea or in a remote area could transmit 'mayday' or "help" on a radio," stated Estonia's Tanagra Space, which supplied the software for the feat. The hope is one day, a satellite could use transcription and AI to alert rescue services for assisting folks in remote zones. The call to play Doom, thankfully, had no other urgency than curiosity — and teamwork, fueled by pizza. OPS-SAT Space Lab managed the experiment on behalf of ESA. Radio amateurs then made six unsuccessful attempts during passes over Poland and Norway, between April and July. The seventh finally reached success under the Oslo Group of the Norwegian Radio Relay League. "We are radio amateurs, with the emphasis on amateurs. Satellite work was not something our club did, and we had no budget for it," representative Eskil Hadland, call sign LB6AJ, said in the Tangara statement. "So we borrowed a line wrongly credited to Pippi Longstocking: 'I have never tried that before, so I should definitely be able to do that.'" The Norwegians spent 59 days and about 7200 NOK or $775 (pizza included) to reach PRETTY, helping make changes to the satellite software to pick up a voice. For example, a raw recording of an attempt on July 3, retransmitted to Earth, showed the spoken words to space were unrecognizable. Further work revealed the satellite's receiver channel was too wide to pick up the voice signal, leading to a fix to narrow the channel. The historic voice command on July 27— in part, "PRETTY play Doom Doom Doom"— came from a rooftop in Oslo, and was spoken at night by Jon Bergli Heier (LB9BJ). PRETTY picked up the transmission, transcribed the command using on-board voice recognition, and then — just like a typical evening gamer—opened up Doom for a play session. A member of the LB9BJ team speaks the command that activated Doom on the OPS-SAT PRETTY satellite while on a rooftop in Oslo, Norway during an evening pass of the spacecraft on July 27, 2026. (Image credit: Truls Johansen (LA7IJ), LA4O) This was no multiplayer gaming situation, but the satellite did create a report of its demon-slaying skills — and its ability to interpret the command. For example, PRETTY generated a "postcard" including a frame of the gameplay, a transcription, and signal diagnostics. The satellite also transmitted its recording of Hadland's command. As anybody who uses voice-recognition software knows, there are challenges in transcriptions: nobody speaks in exactly the same way, and aspects such as accent or background noise can lead to misinterpretations. The satellite also had to contend with Doppler shift

item.title: From “Behind The Scenes” to “Call of My Life”: 5 All-Time Highest-Grossing Nollywood Movies
item.description: Toyin Abraham’s directorial comedy drama Oversabi Aunty is now streaming on Netflix and Kava. Nigerian cinema has witnessed an unprecedented commercial evolution over recent years, with local box office totals soaring past figures once considered unthinkable. From the era when a four-hundred-million-Naira milestone set the nationwide ceiling to an era defined by multi-billion-Naira theatrical runs, audiences across West Africa continue to show up in massive numbers for homegrown storytelling. Here is a look at the five highest-grossing Nollywood blockbusters in history that have continually redefined theatrical success, shattered industry records, and set historic commercial benchmarks across Nigerian cinemas. A Tribe Called Judah (2023) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.40 Billion When this family heist drama landed in Nigerian cinemas on 15 December 2023, few anticipated just how dramatically it would reset the financial ceiling for homegrown features. Directed by Funke Akindele and Tobi Makinde for the Funke Ayotunde Akindele Network (FAAN), the story follows Jedidah Judah—played by Akindele herself—and her five sons from different fathers as they scheme to rob a luxury furniture shop to fund their mother’s life-saving medical care. Supported by a stellar lineup including Timini Egbuson , Jide Kene Achufusi , Uzee Usman , Tobi Makinde , Olumide Oworu , Nse Ikpe Etim , and Genoveva Umeh , the narrative struck a deep chord across multiplexes. By the end of its theatrical run, the project had earned over ₦1.40 Billion, making history as the very first Nollywood title to surpass the ₦1 Billion domestic milestone and cementing Funke Akindele’s status as a formidable box office power. A Tribe Called Judah poster celebrating its historic ₦1 Billion box office milestone. Photo Credit: Filmone/Instagram Everybody Loves Jenifa (2024) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.88 Billion FAAN Studios returned to the festive release window on 13 December 2024 with a comedy-drama co-directed by Funke Akindele and Tunde Olaoye. Centred on the enduring popularity of the lead character, the narrative charts Jenifa’s latest misadventures across global settings, societal expectations, and personal choices, bolstered by on-screen performances from Falz , Layi Wasabi , Patience Ozokwor , and Stan Nze . Building rapidly on its festive debut, the feature went on to generate ₦1.88 Billion in local ticket sales. The milestone surpassed Akindele’s previous commercial record and established an extraordinary streak of back-to-back record-breaking theatrical hits. Funke Akindele and Falz on the ₦1 Billion milestone poster for Everybody Loves Jenifa. Photo Credit: Funke Akindele/Instagram Oversabi Aunty (2025) — Domestic Box Office: ₦1.17 Billion Toyin Abraham made her big-screen directorial debut with this comedy-drama from Toyin Abraham Films, which opened in cinemas nationwide on 19 December 2025. item.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
item.description: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the UN’s chief urged world leaders to “get serious” about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes. Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual two-week climate conference. The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos. “We have entered a new age of climate extremes,” Guterres said in a statement. The UN secretary-general urged leaders to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”. The COP31 opening ceremony opened an hour-and-a-half late without explanation. Negotiators had been locked in discussions late Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda. “This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation. Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient. Inventor said developed countries took a “hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations. A source familiar with the talks said the “climate finance work programme” would be included in the agenda. African countries had also pushed for the agenda to include the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops. The source said there would be no separate agenda point on tripling of adaptation finance but that it would be discussed under other items. A senior European Union official warned last week that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges at COP31. Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The long-term climate outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. – Fossil fuel fight – Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference but raised concerns over how it would work. item.title: AI Slop FM radio experiment puts machines on trial, one dodgy tune at a time
item.description: A Welsh music enthusiast has built an internet radio station that plays AI-generated tunes alongside human-made tracks without telling listeners which is which, to find out whether listeners really hate AI music or just the idea of it. AI Slop FM is the creation of Mike Chaffin, who built and runs the station single-handedly from Ammanford, Carmarthenshire. By stripping away artist names, cover art, and any mention of AI, Chaffin hopes to find out what listeners really think when they have nothing but the music to go on. The free 24/7 station asks listeners to rate tracks from S to E, tag how the music makes them feel, and leave written feedback. The most popular submissions will eventually make it into a weekly chart called the Slop 40, giving creators something that can be hard to come by in the age of streaming: an actual audience. Anyone can submit a track, including human musicians, although Chaffin has already discovered that not all of them are particularly keen on the idea. He told The Register that he had floated the idea to an unsigned musician friend who had sold around 600 albums, but was met with a rather nervous response. "Wh, wh, why would I want to do that?" the musician reportedly asked, according to Chaffin, who said he had never heard his friend stutter before. "It seems that there is a deep rooted fear of AI music in the industry," Chaffin said. The station is still in beta, with Chaffin waiting for enough submissions to fill its schedule across different genres before opening it fully. He's already been pleasantly surprised by the quality of the music submitted, although he still listens to every track to make sure nobody is trying to pass off Bohemian Rhapsody as their own work. Among the early offerings are what Chaffin describes as a developing genre of slightly rude protest songs about HR departments, along with an operatic epic about a blocked toilet. "Some of which are hilarious," he said of the HR songs. As for the toilet opera, it "runs through my head about once a day, whether I like it or not." Chaffin believes the sheer volume of music uploaded to streaming platforms means plenty of perfectly decent tracks never find an audience, whether a person or a machine made them. He hopes AI Slop FM will give some of those overlooked creations a chance to be heard. "You don't have to have published your creations to upload. Just to own the rights," he explained. Tracks that don't make the Slop 40 could still get another outing, with plans for genre-specific stations offering unsuccessful submissions a second chance. The bigger question is what happens when listeners start rating AI-generated music more highly than the human competition, but Chaffin isn't particularly worried about that. "If the machines win then their creators clearly deserve to be heard, deserve an audience. If the musicians win, then that's reassuring for them." item.title: World Entering ‘Age Of Climate Extremes,’ UN Chief Warns
item.description: The world is entering a new reality where climate extremes are the norm, the United Nations chief Antonio Guterres warned Monday, urging leaders at the COP31 climate conference in Turkey to “get serious”. “A supersized El Niño is colliding with a planet already superheated by manmade climate change,” the UN secretary-general said in a statement. “We have entered a new age of climate extremes.” As leaders gathered in Antalya for the UN climate summit, Guterres called on them to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres speaks during the 15th ASEAN – United Nations (UN) Summit at the 47th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Kuala Lumpur on October 27, 2025. (Photo by Chalinee Thirasupa / POOL / AFP) | Chalinee Thirasupa / POOL / AFP His statement came as the UN’s World Meteorological Organisation released a report indicating that 2026 has continued a streak of exceptional global temperatures, melting ice and rising sea levels. Each of the past 12 years has been among the hottest 12 years on record, the agency said, with this year expected to be among the hottest ever. ‘Off The Charts’ “What we are seeing gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts,” WMO chief Celeste Saulo told reporters in Geneva, cautioning that the current exceptionally strong El Niño could unleash more heat and extreme weather well into next year. “We should prepare for another record-breaking year in 2027.” The global average surface temperature between January and September this year was around 1.47 degrees Celsius above the pre-industrial average, the WMO said. And this year’s El Niño — expected to be the strongest since 1950 at least — could push the figure higher by the end of the year. Preliminary data show 2026 ranking among the four hottest years on record, WMO climate information chief John Kenned told reporters, adding though that “with the El Niño developing, we might see when the final numbers come in that we’re close to the top”. The naturally occurring weather phenomenon releases heat from the ocean, which this year has been the warmest ever measured, Saulo pointed out. El Niño is declared when the sea surface temperature is half a degree above average in the tropical Pacific, but from now through January, WMO forecasts “it may be 3.8C above average”, she said. The WMO also reported that the global sea level was the highest on record, freshwater was dwindling and glaciers were continuing a long-term retreat. In 2025, the annual mass loss of ice was enough to fill five Olympic pools every second that year, it said. At the same time, “we are supercharging our weather and El Niño will be a risk multiplier”, Saulo said, warning that “heatwaves, tropical cyclones, and rainstorms are intensifying faster than our historical baselines prepared us for”. item.title: Government offices shut in Osun as NLC directs workers strike
item.description: Government offices in Osun were shut on Monday as workers embark on a three-day strike as directed by the state chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on Sunday. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates to the Osun Government Secretariat and the State House of Assembly in Osogbo were under lock with no workers or business activities ongoing in the premises. Similarly, the Olorunda Local Government Secretariat and Osogbo Local Government Secretariat gates were also locked. Students of public schools in Osogbo were also asked to return home, as teachers in public schools equally joined the strike. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that NLC Chairman in Osun, Christopher Arapasopo, and Secretary, Victor Amusan, in a statement on Sunday, directed all affiliate members of the congress to embark on a three-day sympathy strike with the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE). The NLC leadership explained that the strike followed the expiration of the seven-day ultimatum issued to the Federal and Osun governments over the continued withholding of the state local government statutory allocations. The NLC said that the issues raised concerning the local government allocations had remained unresolved. It said that after exhausting all reasonable avenues and in accordance with the resolutions reached at the emergency meeting of the State Executive Council (SEC) held on Oct. 28, all affiliate members of NLC were directed to embark on strike. item.title: Crime pays: how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus
item.description: Ever since it crashed on to PC and consoles in the late 90s, GTA has been tearing up the game-making rulebook. We explore how its cultural references, rebel spirit and sprawling sense of freedom make it a definitive work of art In the 00s, when the Grand Theft Auto developer Rockstar Games revealed a new project, video game writers from all over the UK would make the journey to the company’s office in London. They would be ushered one by one into a darkened room to sit facing an enormous TV. There would be a dish of sweets on a low bench in front of them but, in the reverential hush that descended, it was never entirely clear if it was acceptable to eat them. After a few moments, the screen would come to life. Rockstar would sometimes begin its presentation not with footage from its new game, but clips from classic movies. This is the context of what we are making, Rockstar was saying, and that is where we belong. Continue reading...

item.title: 'Nazi vanity project': Eagle's Nest in Bavarian Alps a symbol of regime's 'conquest of nature'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Sir Richard Evans, British Historian and Regius Professor Emeritus of History at the University of Cambridge. The controversy surrounding the fate of Adolf Hitler's Eagle's Nest, the Nazi-era mountaintop complex in the Bavarian Alps, raises profound questions about the relationship between architecture, historical memory and political extremism. At the heart of the debate lies a difficult distinction: preserving the material evidence of history is not necessarily the same as preserving the symbols through which a criminal regime sought to glorify itself. "This is a Nazi vanity project," Evans argues and his conclusion is unequivocal: the mountain must be "restored to its natural state."

item.title: From Joeboy to Shenseea & Asake: 5 New Music Videos to Watch This Week
item.description: FOLA and Davido capture a behind-the-scenes moment during the 2am in Toronto video shoot. Photo Credit: FOLA/Instagram The songs have been on repeat, but have you seen the videos? Joeboy , FOLA and Davido , Magixx , Libianca , Shenseea and Asake are among the artistes giving us fresh visuals for their latest releases. From city-night scenes to colourful dance sequences, here are five music videos to press play on. Joeboy – Pretty Girls Joeboy returns with vibrant, upbeat visuals for his latest single, “Pretty Girls”. Directed with a high-energy,sun-soaked aesthetic, the music video captures a lively weekend celebration filled with bold fashion, vibrant choreographies, and colorful backdrop palettes. Joeboy anchors the visuals with his signature smooth charisma, surrounded by dynamic dance routines that perfectly match the track’s bouncy, infectious rhythms. FOLA featuring Davido – 2am in Toronto FOLA connects with Afrobeats powerhouse Davido in the sleek music video for “2am in Toronto”. Capturing the mood of a late-night North American city escapade, the video features atmospheric cinematic lighting,luxury street cruising, and moody skyline views of Toronto. Davido brings his effortless superstar presence to match FOLA’s silky melodies, creating an intimate, nocturnal visual experience that blends high-end lifestyle aesthetics with smooth R&B-infused Afrobeats. Magixx featuring Shoday – Ferawa Mavin Records star Magixx reunites with Shoday to deliver fun, romantic visuals for their playful Afropop collaboration, “Ferawa”. Building on their natural on-screen chemistry, the video features lighthearted storytelling, vivid color-blocked set designs, and witty performance scenes. Magixx’s smooth vocal delivery combined with Shoday’s energetic presence gives the visuals an easygoing, feel-good charm that makes it an instant watch. Libianca featuring Zeeboy – I Know Cameroonian-American singer Libianca delivers a deeply emotional, visually poetic output for “I Know,” featuring Zeeboy. The video blends soulful storytelling with striking artistic imagery, centering around themes of vulnerability, personal peace, and self-reflection. Through soft lighting, intimate close shots, and evocative artistic set pieces, Libianca’s visual direction amplifies the raw depth of her signature Afro-R&B sound. Shenseea featuring Asake – Playtime Jamaican Dancehall queen Shenseea links up with Nigerian superstar Asake in the high-octane music video for “Playtime”. Bridging the worlds of Caribbean vibes and West African rhythms, the visuals are packed with vibrant colors, fiery dance choreography, and striking fashion styling. Asake’s magnetic stage presence matches Shenseea’s bold, energetic delivery, making this cross-continental collaboration a visually thrilling visual experience. item.title: How Seyi Ademeso Turned Awkwardness Into the Meshkiey Brand
item.description: Some people spend years trying to avoid awkward situations. Seyi Ademeso has built a career out of creating them, in the identity of Meshkiey . The content creator has turned everyday social discomfort into a distinctive style of comedy, earning an audience that recognises him for his unconventional approach to skits. But there is more to Seyi than the character who seems willing to embarrass himself for a laugh. Beyond the camera, he is a creative strategist, entrepreneur and businessman with ambitions that stretch far beyond social media. In this exclusive, we sat down with him to talk about the journey, the person behind the persona and what he hopes to build next. Hello Meshkiey. How are you feeling today? I’m feeling good. Honestly, I’m grateful. I’m excited to have this conversation and reflect on the journey. Before Meshkiey became the person people know online, what were you like growing up? I think I’ve always been a very observant person. Even growing up, I noticed little things about people, the way they behaved, the way they spoke, the funny things people did without realising they were funny. I was also quite expressive. I wouldn’t necessarily say I was the loudest person in every room, but I definitely had a personality. I liked making people laugh, and I enjoyed doing things differently. Looking back, I think a lot of the things people now associate with Meshkiey were actually already there. The difference is that I eventually found a platform where I could turn those traits into something creative. When did you start creating, really? I started creating around 2016, and honestly, there wasn’t some grand master plan behind it. I think I just wanted to create. I had a phone, I had ideas, and I was fascinated by what people were doing online. At the time, content creation wasn’t necessarily viewed as a serious career path the way it is today. My early content was very different from what people know me for now. I was experimenting a lot, trying different formats and figuring out what felt natural to me. I didn’t have the polished understanding of branding or storytelling that I have today. I was basically learning in public. I was creating, posting, seeing what people responded to and slowly discovering my voice. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Seyi Ademeso (@meshkiey) Your seemingly awkward and creative style has become a character of its own. When did you realise that the things that might normally be considered unconventional could actually become your creative strength? I think the realisation came gradually. At some point, I noticed that the things I thought were too awkward, too embarrassing or too unconventional were actually the things people remembered. Instead of trying to fit into what I thought a content creator should look like, I started asking myself, “What if I lean completely into this?” That became Meshkiey. The awkwardness stopped being something I needed to hide and became a storytelling tool. I reali

item.title: Memory crunch makes refurbished kit look a lot less secondhand
item.description: Rising memory prices are pushing more customers toward refurbished tech, suppliers say, with warranties of up to three years helping to make secondhand kit a less daunting purchase. Memory costs have more than quadrupled this year as manufacturers prioritize more lucrative high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for servers powering AI datacenters. Many enterprises are keeping equipment longer in an uncertain economy. Ben Caddy, senior analyst at Omdia, said suppliers were linking refresh discussions with opportunities to recover value from customers' aging kit. By 2030, he predicted, 35 percent of "all the hardware sold for the channel will be taken back by partners," driven "by the sheer economic logic of taking equipment back, recovering value, and embracing more circular IT lifecycles." This is already helping some customers "unlock some capital to put towards those [relatively] small refresh plans," he said while hosting a panel on circular IT at last month's Canalys Forums in Barcelona. Refurbished smartphones are growing in popularity, but persuading customers to trade in their old devices remains a constraint on supply. The same applies to PCs and other equipment, said Jon Sansom, MD at GreenSafe IT. "Availability is a challenge," he said. Marcel Joosten, group director of marketing and digital commerce at tech lifecycle specialist XTENTEC, said the company now offers trade-ins when customers buy new kit. "We're actually financing the residual value" at the end of year two, three, or four, when customers return the equipment, he told the audience. XTENTEC collects, refurbishes, rents, and resells equipment, and has an agreement with HP to renovate aging products, with a two or even three-year warranty available as "just an SKU on the list from HP." Joosten said equivalent support, including HP Care Pack services, helped make refurbished equipment more attractive to buyers. Customers want to cut their carbon footprint, and many public and private sector tenders require it. But the "most important thing" for many is trust, said Patrick Molberg, CEO of Advania Finance. "The customers have to trust the refurbished equipment and have to trust the process. And I think one of the things that we have to be better at as a whole is that we kind of need to have a standard methodology regarding verification." Work on verification standards with vendors including HP, Lenovo, and Dell is ongoing, Molberg said. He also argued that lifecycle services should be built into purchasing decisions rather than added three or four years later. Joosten argued that listed US tech companies' focus on quarterly sales and market share can work against refurbishment. "That needs to change," he said. "I think there should be a market share figure for circularity." ®

item.title: African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United
item.description: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson scored after just four minutes for Aston Villa, who twice surrendered two-goal leads in a remarkable 4-4 Premier League draw away to Manchester United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put his side 2-0 ahead against United, but it wasn’t enough to inspire a victory at Old Trafford. When Jackson tapped in after United goalkeeper Senne Lammens palmed the ball into his path, it appeared the 25-year-old’s ninth goal in 14 games in all competitions this term would be the spark for a comfortable Villa win. But in an incredible finale, United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue a draw. YANN GBOHO (Coventry City) The Ivory Coast winger scored his first Premier League goal in a 3-1 defeat at Everton. Gboho, signed from French side Toulouse in September, put Coventry ahead with a composed finish after evading slack defending in the 52nd minute. But Frank Lampard’s team crumbled after the 25-year-old’s strike as Everton scored three times to leave the visitors one point above the relegation zone. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri continued his superb season with another goal to help Santander win 2-1 at Malaga. The 21-year-old bagged his ninth of the campaign with a simple finish to tuck a rebound home into the empty net. Only Raphinha, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal have scored more goals this season in La Liga. ITALY KONAN N’DRI (Lecce) After Angolan Kailonda Gaspar conceded a 60th-minute own goal to give Torino the lead in a clash of bottom-half Serie A clubs, Niger international N’Dri scored to salvage a 1-1 draw for visiting Lecce. The architect of the equaliser was Mali international Lassana Coulibaly. GERMANY EZECHIEL BANZUZI (RB Leipzig) Banzuzi’s goal proved the turning point as he kick-started Leipzig’s recovery to beat Augsburg 5-2 at home in the Bundesliga after conceding inside the opening minute. Anton Kade had Augsburg in front after 36 seconds but Banzuzi levelled in the 33rd minute when he turned a Brajan Gruda pass into the bottom right corner. The 21-year-old Democratic Republic of Congo internnational has two goals and two assists in the league this season. UCHENNA OGUNDU (Augsburg) Ogundu’s first goal in Augsburg colours was a mere consolation as his side crashed at Leipzig. With Leipzig 5-1 up, Augsburg’s Alexis Claude Maurice intercepted the ball and sent his side in the other direction. Fabian Rieder latched on to Claude Maurice’s pass before finding Ogundu, who slid the ball into the bottom corner. FRANCE LASSINE SINAYOKO (Paris FC) Ligue 1’s leading scorer Sinayoko netted after 63 minutes to give third-placed Paris FC a 1-0 win at lowly Auxerre. It was the ninth goal of the campaign in 10 matches for the Mali striker. The post African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume
item.description: US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday. Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections. The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.” “I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday. The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed. “For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television. “We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added. – ‘They had enough’ – Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat. Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.” “Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.” In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms. “They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.” Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September. Iranian state television said the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked overnight Sunday, hours after the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions there. Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war. Outright fighting has largely subsided, but Iran continues in its efforts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global energy supplies, while the US Navy maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. The post Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?
item.description: Tech executive Alice Huang is the woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, according to media reports. Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International. Here is what we know about her and the company: – Who is Alice Huang? – Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia boss, according to the New York Times, which first reported that Jensen Huang was the alleged target of a spy plot. Despite their shared surname, Alice Huang is no relation to the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born head of the world’s most valuable company. The Times, citing people briefed on the surveillance, said that Alice Huang speaks good English and is well connected at the highest level of the global AI chip industry. The sector is highly sensitive as the United States and China race to develop advanced AI systems with potential military applications. An online search brought up a short profile for Alice Huang, with her photo, on a Chinese fund database. It listed previous jobs including at HSBC bank, and as a reporter for Chinese media outlets CCTV and Hunan TV. AFP was unable to verify the contents of the profile, or who had written it, but has attempted to contact the companies cited. – How are the pair connected? – Media reports last week said they had a close relationship, and Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on Sunday he was “deeply sorry” for being “unfaithful to my wife”. One photo from an industry party in 2024, posted on LinkedIn, appears to show the leather jacket-clad Nvidia boss sitting next to a long-haired woman in glitzy jewellery believed to be Alice Huang. The following year, they both attended a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. Alice Huang is also seen following the Nvidia chief as he re-enters the restaurant after talking to journalists outside, running her fingers down his lower back. They later leave the restaurant in the same car. – What is Megaspeed? – US officials concluded last year that Alice Huang was targeting Jensen Huang as a spy, according to the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal. At the time, Alice Huang was said to be a top executive at data centre firm Megaspeed International, which rents out computing power to other companies to train and run AI. item.title: Gunmen kill security operative, three others in Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three residents and a security operative during an attack on Bel village in Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, while several other persons sustained injuries. The attack reportedly occurred at about 9 p.m. on Sunday when the gunmen stormed the community and opened fire on residents. A resident of the community, Mr Bulus Bot, who confirmed the incident, said the attackers invaded the village at night and shot indiscriminately at innocent citizens. “The gunmen stormed the community at about 9 p.m. and opened fire on innocent citizens, leaving some people dead and others injured,” he said. Bot described the incident as a disturbing attack on the community, noting that residents were caught up in the violence when the gunmen opened fire. He said some persons sustained injuries during the attack, adding to the concern among residents over the safety of people in the area. The Publicity Secretary of Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the killings and identified three of the victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. He alleged that a soldier was also among those killed in the attack, bringing the reported death toll to four. Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, and called on security operatives to track down those responsible. He urged security agencies to ensure that the perpetrators were identified and brought to justice, stressing the need for decisive action to prevent further attacks on communities in the area. Efforts to get a reaction from security operatives on the attack were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Dev error bricked 600 PCs, caused $1M CD-ROM write-off
item.description: Welcome to Monday, the day upon which The Register offers a new instalment of " Who, Me? " – our reader-contributed column that shares your stories of messing up, 'fessing up, and somehow finding redress. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Oriel" who told us he once worked for a vendor of small business accounting software. This story comes from a time when software shipped on CD-ROMs and users bought it off the shelf in actual shops. The vendor released a new version each year and always shipped it before a major holiday that's celebrated with a giant meal. Oriel was part of the team whose job it was to get the package ready on time. In the previous year, they flubbed the job because the program didn't always install itself on some PCs running Windows 95 or Windows ME machines system due to registry corruption. "We wanted to increase our successful installation metrics, so in conjunction with the installation team, a key decision was made – by me – to force the updating of registry keys to enable the install," Oriel admitted. In his email to The Register , he asked the portentous question: "What could possibly go wrong?" What went wrong was that not long after the software was shipped, the vendor's support lines started getting calls from customers who complained that after installing the accounting package none of their other software would work. "Installing a new version of our application had borked the customer's machine completely," Oriel wrote. The company decided the best thing to do was to tell affected customers they should go and buy a new PC – and that it would pick up the bill, no questions asked. "In the week prior to the holiday, we replaced over 600 machines," Oriel told The Register . Oriel and his developer colleagues were of course told to fix the problem but couldn't reproduce it nor figure out their mistake. "To get a reproduction case we need a user's machine where the user had created a Windows Registry restore point prior to installing our application," Oriel explained. If the developers could find such a machine, the plan was to roll it back to the restore point, verify everything was in order before the customer installed the update, install the accounting software, and figure out the problem. The company tasked its support agents with finding a customer willing to surrender their PC, which proved difficult because few bothered to create a registry restore point. The day before the holiday, a customer volunteered their machine. This customer was located a few hours away by road, so an engineer got the job of visiting on the morning of the holiday to pick up the stricken machine, give the customer a shiny new system and configure it to their specifications. Said engineer did the job, which took so long he was invited to stay for the holiday meal, then returned to HQ with the broken box. item.title: British people don’t trust Palantir – it’s not too late to reverse the NHS’s dependence on it | Ben Coleman
item.description: We can’t allow our health data to be locked into the control of a US tech firm. It won’t be easy, but next spring the job of clawing it back must begin Ben Coleman is Labour MP for Chelsea and Fulham and a member of the health and social care committee Next March, Palantir’s £330m contract to run NHS England’s federated data platform (FDP) ends. Ministers must decide by Christmas whether to extend it. They should move on from Palantir, and transition to new suppliers that put the NHS in full control of its technology and patient data. I sit on the health and social care committee. In June, we recommended no extension – people don’t trust Palantir , its benefits are contested and other tools could deliver the same or similar advantages. The debate so far has been whether to drop Palantir. The harder question is what replaces it. The tempting solution is to hire a single British firm. But that would not give the NHS the control it lacks: the freedom to switch supplier without losing what it has built. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 9 – Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 9 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch? The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula’s shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch’s head. Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation . What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to — because it has been partly eroded by — the nearby star Rigel . One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image . The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel’s intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth’s daytime sky to appear blue , although the scatterers in planet Earth’s atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen . item.title: ‘Thicky thicky dumb dumb’ satirist Cody Dahler on his viral videos: ‘my material is presented to me on a silver platter!’
item.description: The writer and podcaster on why politics is made to seem more complicated than it is and his mission to unpack world events for everyone Why did you get into comedy? My mum was a professional dancer and always encouraged me to perform. Given that I have zero rhythm, comedy was my other option. She wrote me a poem called Mrs Brown’s Moggy, about a cat that was often very soggy, for my school’s talent show. Because you can’t tell the difference between real and polite laughter at the age of six, I assumed I’d killed my first gig and convinced myself I was born to do nothing else. Where do you find your material? In a world where Robert Jenrick claims Nigel Farage has “ probably done more than almost anybody to stand against racism ”, the answer is that my material is presented to me on a silver platter each morning.
